Amazon Leo is building a global e-commerce experience for Internet Service Provider (ISP) customers, and we need a Software Development Engineer II. You will build the backend-for-frontend layer, the service that sits directly behind the customer-facing surfaces and orchestrates over the many backend systems that make satellite internet work: ordering, payments, billing, equipment and network provisioning, and support. The job is to shape what the frontend needs, route and orchestrate requests across those systems, translate between them, and compose their responses into reliable operations the customer experience can depend on. The core of the work is integration: calling many APIs, handling partial failures gracefully, mapping between different service models, and keeping latency and reliability high across a lot of moving parts. Much of this is built zero-to-one and expanding into new countries, so you will move from ambiguous problems to working products. You will own the full development lifecycle and work closely with frontend, product, and partner service teams. Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing a pull request from a teammate, suggesting improvements to a React component's accessibility and performance. After standup, you pick up a new feature that doesn't have a clear precedent yet, sketching out an approach with your product manager before writing code. In the afternoon, you pair with a designer to refine interaction details for an upcoming launch, then dig into an operational metric that looks off, tracing it to a rendering edge case you fix before it reaches customers. About the team We are part of the Leo Commerce engineering organization at Amazon, building the e-commerce experience for a global ISP customer base. Our team works closely with backend commerce services, product, marketing, and business partners to launch new experiences from scratch. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.</p> <p>All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our<a href="https://gusto.com/about/careers/total-rewards" target="_blank"> <u>Total Rewards philosophy</u></a>.</p> <p>AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.</p></div><p><strong>About the Role:</strong></p> <p>Foundation Insights &amp; Operations (I&amp;O) enables leaders across People, Finance, and Legal &amp; Compliance to move from strategy to execution. We lead high-impact, cross-functional programs, build scalable operating systems, and incubate new capabilities, including AI-native workflows. We are strategic operators, not coordinators: we help frame ambiguous problems, build reusable playbooks, and leave teams stronger than we found them.</p> <p>As an Insights &amp; Operations partner, you'll be strategically aligned to POST, our people technology, HRIS, People Systems Engineering, recruiting operations, and Global Ops teams. POST builds products for employees, and you'll help it operate like a true product org: roadmapping, supporting build prioritization, streamlining how work gets built, and landing launches well with the Gusties who use them. You'll also own comms strategy for POST's employee-facing work, planning what employees hear, from whom, and when, so launches and changes land clearly and not as surprises.</p> <p><strong>About the Team:</strong></p> <p>Foundation I&amp;O is a small, high-leverage team that partners with Foundation leaders across People, Finance, and Legal &amp; Compliance. We organize around programs (for example environment and community, employee relations and People Partner programs, total rewards, and POST) so each person builds real depth, and we build playbooks and operating mechanisms that outlast any single project.</p> <p><strong>Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Maintain the POST roadmap and surface dependencies and tradeoffs</li> <li>Support prioritization conversations with POST leaders by bringing evidence and clear recommendations, without owning the backlog</li> <li>Design and improve intake, planning cadences, and launch checklists</li> <li>Own comms strategy for POST launches and changes, covering audience, sequencing, channels, and timing, in partnership with People Comms and POST leaders</li> <li>Plan launch and adoption work, and report on portfolio status and patterns to People leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>Here’s what we're looking for:</strong></p> <ul> <li>5+ years of People, technology, or operations program or product management experience, including 2+ years driving multi-stakeholder, cross-functional programs end to end</li> <li>Experience with roadmapping and prioritization, ideally for internal or employee-facing technology</li> <li>Experience planning and sequencing communications for employee-facing launches or organizational change</li> <li>A track record of building processes, playbooks, or program infrastructure that teams adopted</li> <li>Comfort working with technical teams and translating between engineering, People, and business partners</li> <li>Strong written communication, including audience-based messaging for employees, managers, and leaders</li> <li>Hands-on use of AI tools in your daily work to speed up synthesis, drafting, and documentation</li> <li>Genuine interest in employee-facing work; prior People team experience is not required</li> <li>Preferred: HRIS or People technology experience (such as Workday), and experience leading change management and adoption for employee-facing launches</li> </ul> <p>Our cash compensation amount for this role is $127,660/yr to $157,447/yr in Denver &amp; most major metro locations, and $154,895/yr to $191,037/yr for San Francisco &amp; New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><hr> <p>At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Achieving commercial success with Terran R will unlock new&nbsp;opportunities to advance science, exploration, and innovation, pioneering progress that reaches beyond&nbsp;the known.</span></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">Joining Relativity means becoming part of something where autonomy, ownership, and impact exist at every level. Here, you're not just executing tasks; you're solving problems that haven’t been solved before, helping develop a rocket, a factory, and a business from the ground up. Whether you’re in propulsion, manufacturing, software, avionics, or a corporate function, you’ll collaborate across teams, shape decisions, and see your work come to life in record time. Relativity is a place where creativity and </span><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">technical rigor go hand in hand, and your voice will help define the stories we’re writing together. Now&nbsp;is a unique moment in time where it’s early enough to leave your mark on the product, the process, and&nbsp;the culture, but far enough along that Terran R is tangible and picking up momentum. The most&nbsp;meaningful work of your career is waiting. Join us.</span></p></div><h2 class="mt-6 mb-2 font-semibold text-2xl" data-streamdown="heading-2"><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">About the Team:</span></h2> <p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">The Factory Platform team is building the digital backbone for all engineering, manufacturing, test, launch, and data review operations at Relativity. Each day we are getting to know our users in every department of the company, defining the core abstractions Relativity is using to scale our vehicle program. Like an operating system for manufacturing, our software enables users to understand, make decisions about, and command the factory.</span></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">Every engineer on our team owns a core part of our system. As an engineer on our team, you will be responsible for understanding your software system and the domain area so you can make informed technical decisions about how to evolve the system over time.</span></p> <p><span style="font-family: arial, helvetica, sans-serif; font-size: 10pt;">In an environment where everyone has access to AI, our team sees good software as a castle surrounded by a marketplace. In this metaphor, the castle represents a core database and APIs with all the domain objects and critical workflows relevant to the business. jobs.jd_excerpt: Software Engineer, Systems & Infrastructure Our mission is to create high-quality training data and evaluations so Meta's AI models become and stay state-of-the-art. Our center of gravity is the hardest part of that problem: software that runs on real devices, under real power and timing constraints. Today's models are genuinely weak there, and it's one of the few gaps you cannot scrape your way out of — it takes real devices, real firmware, real bring-up, and a working loop around all of it. That's the center of gravity, not the boundary. jobs.jd_excerpt:
The Data Intelligence team is a new function within Amazon Customer Service (CS). We own the end-to-end process of defining, building, implementing, and monitoring a comprehensive data strategy. We also develop and apply Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), Machine Learning (ML), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) to enhance customer service associate and customer experiences. As an Applied Scientist, you'll own the definition and implementation of customer-focused, AI-driven innovation in Amazon Customer Service globally, leveraging GenAI, ML, and/or NLP to transform complex business requirements and customer needs into innovative technology solutions. Your expertise will be key in shaping data-driven strategies and addressing complex data challenges. With your expertise in AI, text analysis, embeddings, language modeling, you'll design and develop scalable AI-powered technology solutions, prioritize initiatives, drive data-driven insights, and deliver business impact. This position will advance applied science best practices, leverage data and AI to drive customer experience improvements, and set new global standards for customer experience. This role requires you to work with a cross-functional team, including scientists, engineers, and product managers, to develop scalable and maintainable AI solutions for both structured and unstructured data. The ideal candidate has strong technical skills in AI techniques, excellent written documentation skills, and experience with big data technologies. Success in this role requires combining deep business knowledge with hands-on technical skills to solve customer problems and address complex technical challenges. Key job responsibilities - Develop innovative solutions to complex problems. - Apply technical expertise to implement novel algorithms and modeling solutions, in collaboration with other scientists and engineers. - Analyze data and define metrics to identify actionable insights and measure improvements in customer experience. - Communicate results and insights to both technical and non-technical audiences through written reports, presentations, and internal/external publications. - Collaborate with product management and engineering teams to integrate and optimize models in production systems. A day in the life A typical day as an Applied Scientist in the Data Intelligence team involves combining business expertise with hands-on problem-solving in ML and AI. The role encompasses tackling complex data initiatives, ensuring alignment with customer needs and business objectives, and translating business requirements into practical AI-driven solutions. Working collaboratively with cross-functional teams, this position involves designing and enhancing AI models, focusing on efficiency, precision, and scalability. Daily activities include ensuring data quality, monitoring model performance, and generating actionable insights from vast amounts of information. Each day presents opportunities to resolve complex technical challenges, advance important AI projects, and conceive innovative ways to leverage data in transforming the customer experience About the team The Data Intelligence team is a new function within Amazon Customer Service. We develop and apply Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), Machine Learning (ML), and Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to enhance customer service associate and customer experiences.

- Experience using Unix/Linux - Experience in professional software development Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. You'll use machine learning to improve how our robots plan, scan, and act. ML problems.</li> <li>Train models that work with classical methods, such as initial guesses and learned costs for trajectory optimization, plan quality and feasibility predictors, and learned collision models.</li> <li>Develop viewpoint planning policies that choose where and how to scan, and predict scan quality before the robot commits.</li> <li>Apply imitation learning, reinforcement learning, and generative models such as diffusion and flow matching where they outperform classical baselines.</li> <li>Build production ML pipelines: datasets from fleet logs and simulation, training, and metrics.</li> <li>Evaluate models in the loop, with offline metrics that predict gains on the robot, failure-mode analysis, and calibrated confidence that determines when the system information-theoretic planning.</li> <li>GPU inference optimization (CUDA, TensorRT, ONNX).</li> <li>Simulation and sim-to-real transfer (Isaac Lab, MuJoCo).</li> <li>Publications at RSS, CoRL, ICRA, Woven by Toyota is enabling Toyota’s once-in-a-century transformation into a mobility company. Inspired by a legacy of innovating for the benefit of others, our mission is to challenge the current state of mobility through human-centric innovation — expanding what “mobility” means and how it serves society.   Our work centers on four pillars: Automated driving technologies; Arene, our software development platform for software-defined vehicles; Woven City, a test course for mobility; and Cloud & AI, the digital infrastructure powering our collaborative foundation. Business-critical functions empower these teams to execute, and together, we’re working toward one bold goal: a world with zero accidents and enhanced well-being for all. jobs.jd_excerpt: Brief Description Integrity. Care. Trust. Compassion. Expertise. Do these words resonate with you? These values of Builders culture create success in all we do. We strive to provide deeply supportive partnerships to our customers, agents, and each other. Builders is proud to be named among the Great Places to Work. Our award-winning culture has earned top marks in Company Direction, Employee Appreciation, Work-Life Balance, Leadership, and Compensation and Benefits. Our strong culture keeps us Built Strong in a forever-changing world, and our AM Best A Rating is evidence of our financial strength. Position Summary The Data Engineer is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining data pipelines that power the company’s Azure Databricks lakehouse for its property and casualty insurance business. Using technologies such as Delta Lake, Unity Catalog, Lakeflow pipelines, and Databricks SQL, the Data Engineer delivers reliable, high-quality, well-tested, and well-documented data to support key business functions, including underwriting, claims, actuarial, and finance. A key responsibility is developing and supporting data pipelines for the phased migration of data from Guidewire and legacy policy, claims, and billing systems into the Azure Databricks lakehouse. The Data Engineer ensures solutions align with the Unity Catalog governance framework and adhere to the engineering standards and best practices established by the Data Engineering Lead. The role also emphasizes knowledge sharing, technical ownership, and long-term sustainability by progressively assuming responsibility for contractor-developed pipelines, strengthening internal expertise, and building lasting in-house platform capabilities. Responsibilities Build pipelines for the phased data migration from Guidewire (PolicyCenter, ClaimCenter, BillingCenter) and legacy systems into the lakehouse on Azure Databricks, including historical loads, incremental/CDC (Change Data Capture) loads and reconciliation. Develop bronze and silver layer transformations in PySpark and Spark SQL on Delta Lake, following the medallion architecture. Support modeling of property and casualty insurance data: policies, insured risks and exposures, coverages, endorsements, premiums, claims, reserves, payments and recoveries. Integrate third-party data sources such as geospatial and weather data. Schedule and run production pipelines with Databricks Workflows (Lakeflow Jobs) or Azure Data Factory, including job dependencies, parameters, retries and alerting; investigate and resolve pipeline failures. Apply Unity Catalog controls defined by the Data Engineering Lead and Data Governance lead, including permissions, PII (Personally Identifiable Information) masking, tags and lineage. Implement data quality checks, error handling and monitoring. Tune pipeline performance and cost, including partitioning, liquid clustering and right-sized job compute. Use Git version control (GitHub or Bitbucket) and CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) with Databricks Asset Bundles to version, review and deploy code across development, test and production. Write documentation and runbooks, take part in code reviews, and take ownership of contractor-built pipelines over time. Perform other duties as assigned. Qualifications Associate degree or an equivalent combination of education and experience Certification in Databricks engineering Three or more years in data engineering, including one or more years hands-on with Databricks (PySpark, Spark SQL, Delta Lake) Experience with property and casualty insurance data, ideally Guidewire data; experience migrating data from legacy source systems Knowledge of Python/PySpark and SQL (Structured Query Language) Knowledge of Unity Catalog: permissions, row/column-level security and lineage Experience with incremental loading patterns such as CDC, MERGE, SCD (Slowly Changing Dimension) and Auto Loader Knowledge of data modeling, including dimensional modeling Experience scheduling and monitoring pipelines with Databricks Workflows and/or Azure Data Factory Experience with Git-based version control (GitHub or Bitbucket), including branching, pull request reviews and Databricks Git folders Experience with Azure data services such as ADLS (Azure Data Lake Storage) Gen2, Azure Data Factory and Key Vault Knowledge of CI/CD basics (Databricks Asset Bundles, Azure DevOps, GitHub Actions or Bitbucket Pipelines) Experience with streaming (Structured Streaming, Event Hubs) Experience with API (Application Programming Interface) and integration tools such as MuleSoft is an added advantage Let’s talk benefits! jobs.jd_excerpt: <h3>Data Scientist (Senior Staff, Staff, &amp; Senior roles available)</h3> <h5><strong>About the company</strong></h5> <p>In the coming decades, demand for critical minerals such as copper, lithium, and cobalt will continue to grow. These minerals are needed to build electric infrastructure, vehicles, data centers, and electronics. However, the mining industry is making 10x fewer discoveries per dollar spent on exploration compared to 30 years ago because the easy-to-find, near surface deposits have largely been discovered.</p> <p>KoBold was founded to be the first AI native mineral exploration, mine development, and technology development company. Our goal is to turn mineral exploration into a repeatable science to discover the minerals the world needs—by integrating artificial intelligence, human intelligence, and new technology. Our multidisciplinary teams of data scientists, engineers, and geologists work together to build data systems, design new sensors, and establish industry-leading workflows to develop and test subsurface predictions on our exploration projects.</p> <p>Our first discovery, Mingomba, is a high-grade copper deposit in Zambia, found after spending materially less than industry average. We are developing Mingomba with the same technical rigor that we apply to exploration. The Mingomba team brings together mine and processing engineers, geologists, data scientists, software engineers, and community, health &amp; safety, construction, and operations specialists. By combining industry knowledge and cutting edge technology, we are developing Mingomba into a world class project that has safer and more predictable outcomes for ourselves, partners, and communities. It is expected to create thousands of good jobs for generations.</p> <p>KoBold runs exploration programs in eight countries, all with the potential for another discovery.</p> <p>KoBold is privately held; investors include institutional asset managers T. Rowe Price and Canada Pension Plan Investments; technology venture capitalists Andreessen Horowitz, Breakthrough Energy Ventures, BOND Capital, Durable Capital, StepStone, and Standard Investments; and strategic natural resources companies BHP and Mitsubishi.</p> <p>We are hiring a Data Scientists to help accelerate our mission.</p> <p><strong>About the position</strong></p> <p>In this role, you will build predictive models and apply a wide range of scientific computing, statistical, and physics-based methods to find places where there is evidence of ore-forming processes at work and to predict the locations of ore-grade mineralization in 2D and 3D. You will help build a worldwide dataset that underlies our exploration program, with careful attention to identifying and quantifying uncertainty in the data and in our predictions. You will create models and develop software to accelerate discovery of critical battery metals.</p> <p>You will join an outstanding team of data scientists and engineers and will work closely with KoBold’s world-renowned geoscientists to incorporate our best understanding of the chemical and physical processes that create ore deposits. Working with your geoscience colleagues, you will create 2D and 3D geologic predictions, identify exploration targets, design field programs to collect data, and use that data to reduce the uncertainty in our predictions and guide the next phase of field work.</p> <p>Ultimately, your role is to help KoBold make valuable discoveries by building data tools to solve scientific problems. As one of the early members of this team, you will help build these tools from the ground up.</p> <p><strong>Responsibilities</strong></p> <p>The Data Scientist will:</p> <ul> <li>Help develop KoBold’s proprietary software exploration tools.</li> <li>Find and curate&nbsp; geophysical, geochemical, geologic, and geographic data and integrate it into KoBold’s proprietary data system.</li> <li>Build models to make statistically valid predictions about the locations of compositional anomalies within the Earth’s crust.</li> <li>Create effective visualizations for evaluating model performance and enabling rapid interaction with the underlying data and key features.</li> <li>Develop and apply data processing, statistical, and physics-based techniques to geoscientific data — from computer vision to geophysical inversions — and use the results to guide our targeting efforts and inform our acquisition and exploration decisions.</li> <li>Present to and collaborate with our external partners and stakeholders.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Qualifications</strong></p> <p>A great Data Scientist candidate will have:</p> <p>Technical skills, including extensive experience with:</p> <ul> <li>Python’s data science packages and general software engineering practices.</li> <li>Collaborative software development (git), and familiarity with software engineering best practices like unit test / integration test suites, and CICD pipelines.</li> <li>Cloud computing resources.</li> <li>Building predictive models, applying them to different problems, and evaluating and interpreting the results.</li> <li>Data from a variety of physical systems.</li> <li>Geospatial analyses and visualizations.</li> </ul> <p>Technical knowledge:</p> <ul> <li>Broad skills in and knowledge of applied statistics and Bayesian inference</li> <li>Substantial understanding of machine learning algorithms</li> </ul> <p>Training and work experience:</p> <ul> <li>An advanced degree in the physical sc

jobs.jd_excerpt: Overview Acuity Inc. is seeking a highly skilled Data Engineer to join our Engineering Team, helping drive the design and delivery of AWS cloud-scale data platforms for federal clients. This role requires knowledge and/or experience with Spark, Delta Lake, and distributed data pipelines on Databricks. The ideal candidate brings both engineering and strategic insight into enterprise data modernization. Why Acuity? Are you ready to use your expertise in the areas of IT Modernization, Data Enablement, and Hyperautomation to make a real difference? Join Acuity, Inc., a technology consulting firm that supports federal agencies. We combine industry partnerships and long-term federal experience with innovative technical leadership to support our customers’ critical missions. Responsibilities Build and maintain scalable PySpark-based data pipelines in Databricks notebooks to support ingestion, transformation, and enrichment of structured and semi-structured data. Design and implement Delta Lake tables optimized for ACID compliance, partition pruning, schema enforcement, and query performance across large datasets. Develop ETL and ELT workflows that integrate multiple source systems into a centralized, query-optimized data warehouse architecture. Leverage Spark SQL and DataFrame APIs to implement business rules, dimensional joins, and aggregation logic aligned to warehouse modeling best practices. Collaborate with data architects and engineers to implement cloud-native data solutions on AWS using S3, Glue, RDS, and IAM for secure, scalable storage and access control. Optimize pipeline performance through intelligent partitioning, caching, broadcast joins, and adaptive query tuning. Deploy and version data engineering assets using Git-integrated development workflows and automate deployment with CI/CD tools such as GitLab or Jenkins. Monitor pipeline health, job execution, and cluster utilization using native Databricks tools and AWS CloudWatch, identifying bottlenecks and optimizing cost-performance tradeoffs. Conduct technical discovery and mapping of legacy source systems, identifying required transformations and designing end-to-end data flows. Implement governance practices including metadata tagging, data quality validation, audit logging, and lineage tracking using platform-native features and custom logic. Support ad hoc data access requests, develop reusable data assets, and maintain shared notebooks that meet operational reporting and analytics needs across teams. Qualifications 4+ years of experience in data engineering and Agile analytics 4+ years of experience creating software for retrieving, parsing and processing structured and unstructured data 2+ years of experience building scalable ETL and ELT workflows for reporting and analytics 2 + years experience building enterprise data engineering solutions in the cloud, with preferred experience with cloud native technologies from AWS and Databricks Experience with data quality, validation frameworks, and storage optimization strategies BA or BS degree Clearance Requirement Must be US Citizen with an ability to obtain and maintain US Suitability Min USD $120,000.00/Yr. jobs.jd_excerpt: Company Description Etsy is the global marketplace for unique and creative goods. We build, power, and evolve the tools and technologies that connect millions of entrepreneurs with millions of buyers around the world. As an Etsy employee, you will tackle unique, meaningful, and large-scale problems alongside passionate coworkers, all the while making a rewarding impact and Keeping Commerce Human. We believe exceptional companies are built by exceptional teams, and we're intentional about it. That means hiring great people, setting them up for success from day one, and giving them real reasons to grow their careers here. We invest in development that goes beyond promotions, and we foster the trust and relationships that help people do their best work together. What's the role? We're hiring Machine Learning Engineers at the Senior and Staff levels to join one of our Search and Discovery teams: Search Ads, Recommendations Ranking, or Search Retrieval. You will build user-centric ML systems for a two-sided marketplace with 90+ million buyers, 6+ million sellers, and hundreds of millions of unique, handmade, and vintage listings. We're looking for people who are product- and delivery-driven and passionate about applying ML innovations (ranking, retrieval, deep learning, reinforcement learning, LLMs, and more) to improve the Etsy buyer and seller experience. You'll own models end-to-end, from data and feature pipelines through training, evaluation, and production serving, and validate their impact through live A/B experiments on Etsy.com and the Etsy app. Team placement is based on your background, level, and interests, and will be discussed during the interview process. This is a full-time position reporting to the Engineering Manager of the team you join. What’s this team like at Etsy? We Apply Cutting-edge Machine Learning, Deep Learning, And Information Retrieval Techniques To High-impact Problems At Etsy Scale. Depending On Your Experience, You May Be Considered For One Of The Following Teams Search Ads: Builds the ML systems behind our sponsored search product, including retrieval, ranking, ad allocation, and user engagement modeling. We ensure the right ads reach the right buyers, personalize the ad experience to each buyer's journey, and help sellers get the most from their advertising budgets, all on a pipeline that scales to our 90+ million buyers and sellers. Recommendations Ranking: Develops ML models that understand buyers, personalize, and rank recommendations across Etsy.com and the Etsy app. Work includes user modeling, personalized ranking, multi-objective optimization, intent and lifecycle prediction, and keeping feeds fresh and reactive to user actions, emerging trends, and seasonal shifts. Search Retrieval: Builds efficient, scalable, and intelligent retrieval systems that surface the most relevant listings from a catalog of over a hundred million unique items. We combine lexical matching, semantic retrieval, and hybrid models to power the first step inEtsy's search stack, using techniques such as dual-encoder models, vector similarity search, and query expansion. What does the day-to-day look like? Work cross-functionally with software engineers, applied scientists, data scientists, product managers, designers, and analytics partners, and communicate your ideas and model capabilities clearly to each. Apply the latest advances in machine learning and information retrieval to improve relevance, personalization, and buyer and seller engagement. Prototype, optimize, and productionize large-scale ML models, owning the path from data and feature pipelines through training, evaluation, serving, and monitoring. Design and run A/B experiments (online and offline) to validate the effectiveness, efficiency, latency, and buyer impact of ML models and pipelines. Investigate and resolve nuanced issues in model and system behavior, and measure and improve our products with product and analytics partners. Depending on your team, work on problems such as retrieval and ranking for sponsored search, ad allocation, user modeling, personalized ranking, multi-objective optimization, intent prediction, dual-encoder and hybrid retrieval, and large-scale indexing and serving. Of course, this is just a sample of the kinds of work this role will require! You should assume that your role will encompass other tasks, too, and that your job duties and responsibilities may change from time to time at Etsy's discretion, or otherwise applicable with local law. Qualities that will help you thrive in this role are: A track record of applying statistical and machine learning techniques to real-world problems. Expertise or experience in one or more of: information retrieval, search, recommendations, ads, natural language processing, deep learning, multi-modal learning, or reinforcement learning. Hands-on experience training, deploying, monitoring, debugging, and iterating on production ML systems in search, recommendation, and/or ads. Production experience building large-scale ML systems in Python, Java, Scala, or similar languages, with modern ML frameworks such as PyTorch or TensorFlow/TFX. The ability to write and manipulate data at large scale, and to write understandable, testable, maintainable code. The ability to create requirements and lead your team from design through delivery. A collaborative, empathetic approach, with clear and constructive communication across disciplines. Care about the implications of your work on end users. M.S. or Ph.D. in Computer Science or a related engineering field with at least two years of practical machine learning experience, or equivalent experience. Compensation & Benefits In addition to salary, you'll be eligible for an equity package, an annual performance bonus, and our competitive benefits that support you and your family. jobs.jd_excerpt: Why Rogo Our mission is to transform global finance by empowering professionals at the world's top investment banks, private equity funds, and investment firms with AI that delivers unparalleled speed, accuracy, and insight. We're not just improving financial workflows; we're redefining them. This is a unique opportunity to join a generational company driving transformation in one of the most important industries in the world. With a rapidly growing, global client base, proven product-market fit, and backing from world-class investors, we are scaling quickly and defining a new category of enterprise AI. Our team is sharp, motivated, and deeply committed to Rogo’s mission. We take ownership of complex problems and stay relentlessly focused on our users. If you thrive in a fast-paced environment, demand excellence, and want to help build the future of finance, we invite you to join us. The Role Analytics at Rogo defines the metrics, runs the pipelines behind them, and turns both into decisions and a better product. We’re hiring a Data Engineer to take full ownership of our Analytics infrastructure and build it into something that scales confidently with the company. This is a hands-on, high-leverage role: pipelines, orchestration, and reliability. If you are an experienced data engineer excited about how your role can evolve at an AI-native organization, this is the opportunity for you. In many ways this is also a product role. Rogo productizes how we use our own data — many of our Analytical features began as internal analytics work. You will be expected to know the product as well as any engineer here, because the systems you build both measure it and support its development. We expect everyone at Rogo to take ownership of making our product better for our users. What You Will Own Own analytics infrastructure: the ETL pipelines, Snowflake, dbt models, orchestration, and the reliability of all of it. Analytics evals: design and run the evaluation and testing layer for our agentic analytics surfaces — internal agents that answer thousands of questions a quarter, and the customer-facing analytics our enterprise admins rely on. This is one of the defining problems of doing analytics at an AI company. Own core KPIs: the definitions, the pipelines that produce them, and the documentation that makes them legible. When a number moves, you can say whether the pipeline broke, the definition changed, or the business moved. Know the product inside and out: develop the same depth of product understanding as any engineer or salesperson at Rogo. Turn internal work into product: partner with engineering and product where our analytics infrastructure becomes a customer-facing feature. Pick up a lane of analytics work: as the foundation solidifies, take a domain of your own and go deep, so the team’s judgment grows alongside its infrastructure. What You Will Need 5+ years of professional experience in data engineering, analytics engineering, or a closely related role, with a track record of owning production data systems. Deep SQL proficiency and fluency in a modern cloud data warehouse (Snowflake preferred) Hands-on dbt experience: models, tests, macros, incremental strategies, and a real point of view on what makes a well-structured transformation layer. Strong Python for pipeline and transformation work, and comfort with orchestration and modern ETL tooling. You have a real point of view on keeping a fast refresh cadence as event volume geometrically increases with our business: partitioning strategies, incremental model design, storage tiering, etc. Genuine fluency with AI products. You’ve used agentic tools seriously and have a working picture of what happens between a question and an answer: retrieval, tool calls, model turns, and where cost accrues. Real curiosity about the business. You care about and take ownership of what a number means, not only that the job ran. Comfort operating with autonomy across multiple stakeholders and domains. Bonus Growth-stage experience, or familiarity with the scale of data Rogo will be handling twelve months from now. Experience building evals or test harnesses for LLM-powered systems. Experience with single- and multi-tenant customer architectures. Familiarity with Salesforce, Intercom, or usage-based billing data models (Metronome or similar). Experience with third-party financial or B2B data vendors (LSEG, FactSet, Crunchbase, ZoomInfo, Apollo, or similar). Background in financial services, enterprise SaaS, or vertical AI. Who You Are You thrive in fast-paced environments. You are high-intensity and care a lot about what you do, and you're ecstatic to work at a startup. You are ambitious. You have fun solving problems that others think are impossible. You are curious. You find joy in learning about AI, technology, and finance. You are an owner. You are autonomous, self-directed, and comfortable working with ambiguity. You are collaborative, organized, thoughtful, and kind. Why Join Rogo? Up and to the right: Rogo has strong product adoption with the world's leading financial institutions, and we are still early. The upside is enormous. Extraordinary team: we take talent density seriously. You'll do the best work of your career alongside some of the sharpest people in AI and finance. A one-of-one problem: bringing AI to the core of how Wall Street works is one of the most ambitious, technically demanding, and consequential problems today. There is nowhere else you can work on it at this scale. Real ownership: You'll own real surface area and watch the world's most sophisticated users rely on your work. Always at the frontier: we work at the edge of what the best models can do and turn it into products people trust. If you're obsessed with AI, this is where it's happening.

Why You Might Be a Good Fit You enjoy translating ambiguous clinical questions into clear, actionable data models and dashboards. You have a solid foundation in healthcare analytics and understand the nuances of clinical and operational data. jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><h2><strong>COMPANY PROFILE</strong></h2> <p>CodeAI is an education innovation nonprofit dedicated to the vision that every student in every school has the opportunity to learn about artificial intelligence (AI) and computer science (CS) as part of their core K-12 education. We increase participation in AI+CS education by reaching students of all backgrounds where they are — at their skill level, in their schools, and in ways that inspire them to keep learning, with a focus on increasing participation by young women and students from other underrepresented groups. The leading provider of K-12 AI+CS education curriculum across the globe, CodeAI also organizes the annual Hour of AI campaign, building on the legacy of the Hour of Code, which has engaged more than 15% of all students in the world!</p> <h2><strong>A unifying approach in a divided world</strong></h2> <p>CodeAI's global role in the K-12 computer science movement is only possible because we use a unifying approach across diverse and often divided stakeholders. Core responsibilities Clean and organize data from approved sources. Build recurring reports and simple dashboards. Verify data quality and investigate unusual results. jobs.jd_excerpt: Description Are you excited to figure out not just what is happening but why — and to help build a delivery business that's still taking shape? We're looking for a Data Scientist who thrives on ambiguity and wants to own measurement, modeling, and experimentation across how customers experience Amazon's drone-delivery service. Your work will span the full data-science toolkit: designing and analyzing experiments (A/B tests), deep-diving customer-experience issues to find root causes, building propensity and behavioral models, forecasting demand, and applying causal methods to understand what actually drives our metrics. You'll work with large, evolving operational and customer datasets; partner closely with data engineers, scientists, and business stakeholders; and translate rigorous analysis into clear, decision-ready recommendations. Because the business is early and moving fast, you'll help define the right problems as much as solve them — with real room to explore new methods and shape how we measure and improve as we scale. If you're a curious, collaborative problem-solver who's energized by turning complex, ambiguous data into insight and clear direction, we'd love to hear from you. Key job responsibilities Design and execute data science solutions using a range of methodologies—including machine learning, statistical modeling, and generative AI techniques—to address business problems where the approach is not immediately clear. Acquire, transform, and validate large, evolving operational and customer datasets dive deep to investigate anomalies and data quality; and partner with data engineers to bring models and metrics into production. Design, run, and analyze experiments (A/B and quasi-experimental studies) to measure impact, size opportunities, and guide product and operational decisions. Deep-dive customer-experience issues and metric movements to identify root causes — the why behind the what, including how our metrics and their drivers relate and translate findings into clear, actionable recommendations. Communicate complex analyses to technical and non-technical audiences, earn the trust of senior leaders, and influence roadmap and prioritization decisions with your recommendations. Own your workstream end-to-end, from problem definition through delivery and ongoing measurement partnering across data engineering, product, and business teams as the business scales. A day in the life You might start your morning reviewing model performance metrics before joining a working session with engineers to refine a data pipeline. After lunch, you could be prototyping a new machine learning approach, running experiments, and comparing results against baseline models. Later, you might present preliminary findings to business partners, translating statistical outputs into plain-language recommendations. You will regularly participate in team discussions, scientific reviews, and mentoring conversations that keep you learning and growing. jobs.jd_excerpt: Description As a Data Engineer you will enable data-driven decision making within the Amazon Web Services Data Center Infrastructure Operations organization. The Infrastructure Operations Team is responsible for planning, implementing, monitoring and continuously improving the global Amazon Data Center infrastructure. The team supports all aspects of the Data Center based organizations, including but not limited to : Safety, Security, maintenance, operations, logistics, engineering and equipment management. Key job responsibilities Design, develop, and maintain ETL pipelines to ingest data into the data warehouse and data lake Create and optimize logical data models that drive physical design for the Infrastructure Operations organization Implement data quality measures and ongoing monitoring to ensure data integrity Build scalable, efficient, and maintainable data solutions that support business intelligence needs Optimize data storage and query performance across various data platforms Develop automated processes to replace manual data operations Collaborate with business stakeholders to understand data and reporting requirements Translate business questions into data solutions that drive decision-making Mentor and develop peers in data engineering best practices Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and team planning Improve self-service access to data for business users Enhance code quality and dependency management Automate manual processes to increase efficiency Identify and resolve root causes of complex data problems A day in the life At AWS, the Data Engineer fully embraces the "You Build It, You Own It" philosophy, taking complete ownership of data solutions from conception through deployment and ongoing maintenance. You design architectures, implement pipelines, and remain responsible for their health and evolution as business needs change. Each day begins with reviewing pipeline alerts and data quality metrics, followed by a 15-30 minute team stand-up to align on priorities and discuss blockers. You'll spend time monitoring infrastructure, reviewing logs for ETL pipeline health and data lake performance, then dedicate time to address stakeholder queries and prioritizing incoming requests via email, Slack and intake forms. The majority of your time is spent developing and maintaining ETL pipelines that ingest infrastructure operational data from global data centers, which includes writing code, debugging issues, optimizing queries, and implementing quality checks. The role requires frequent context switching between developing new data models, supporting existing infrastructure, and consulting on data utilization. Key challenges you'll tackle include unifying and understanding fragmented data from diverse data center systems, enabling infrastructure monitoring, supporting analytics for capacity planning, driving optimization through data insights, automating manual processes, creating self-service access for business users, maintaining quality across massive datasets, ensuring compliance with strict security requirements, designing for scale as AWS expands globally, and modernizing legacy systems to reduce technical debt. About The Team Our team builds the data foundation behind AWS's global data center operations. We turn raw operational signals into trusted data products, dashboards, and APIs that technicians, site leaders, and executives use every day to keep infrastructure safe, reliable, and efficient. jobs.jd_excerpt: Fingerprint empowers enterprises to detect and stop online fraud with the world's most accurate device intelligence. We lead our industry with bleeding-edge identification capabilities and work on turning new ideas and discoveries in the fraud detection space into reality. Our customers range from innovative startups to leading enterprise companies, including Plaid, Dropbox, and Booking.com. Fingerprint is a globally dispersed, 100% remote company. We were named on on the 2026 Forbes Best Startup Employers list and ranked #803 on the 2026 Inc. 5000 list of America's fastest-growing private companies. We have raised $77M and are backed by Craft Ventures (Tesla, Facebook, Airbnb ), Nexus Venture Partners ( Postman, Apollo.io, MinIO, Druva) and Uncorrelated Ventures ( Redis, Rollbar, Gradle). Are you passionate about data analytics and eager to work on large-scale projects? Fingerprint is looking for a Data Analyst to join our Identification Accuracy Team. You will be the team's go-to analyst for questions about how accurately we identify browsers and devices: investigating accuracy questions from Customer Success and Sales, building the reporting and dashboards those teams rely on, and turning repeat requests into self-service tools. Our Identification API Product processes approximately 1 billion requests per month, so you will work hands-on with large-scale event data and the models behind it. Responsibilities: Act as the first point of contact for identification accuracy questions from Customer Success, Sales Engineering and Product: investigate reported false positives and false negatives, find the root cause, and explain it in terms customers and internal teams can act on. Lead accuracy analyses for strategic customers and prospects, including building customer-specific metrics from the customer's own data (for example, account IDs) when our standard metrics don't fit their use case. Design, build, and maintain dashboards and reports that support Customer Success and the Sales Engineering organizations, such as customer accuracy health reports and weekly book-of-business summaries. Build self-service tools, including AI-assisted ones, that let teams answer routine accuracy questions without waiting on an analyst, and drive their internal adoption. Model and maintain analytics data with dbt on ClickHouse (aggregates, incremental models and tests) so dashboards stay fast, trustworthy and documented. Monitor Identification accuracy, detect anomalies, and analyze trends in time-series data, raising issues before customers notice them. Document findings and investigation playbooks so knowledge is reusable across the team. Foster an engineering-focused, data-driven culture within the Fingerprint team by sharing tools and knowledge on effective data analytics approaches. This role includes participation in a shared on-call rotation. The schedule will be communicated in advance, and we strive to balance coverage equitably while minimizing off-hours disruptions. Qualifications: Proficiency in English for clear communication within an international remote team. BS/MS in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent work experience. 3+ years of experience in Data Analytics, Analytics Engineering, or Data Science. Strong SQL skills, including CTEs, window functions, and writing efficient queries over large event-level datasets. Strong foundation in statistics for designing metrics, sizing impact, and telling a real change from noise. Practical experience with analytical storage solutions such as Clickhouse, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Databricks, etc. Experience building dashboards and using data visualization tools like Apache Superset, Tableau, Metabase, Looker, etc. Strong coding skills with clean, maintainable code; experience with version control (Git) and collaborative development practices Experience investigating data discrepancies and root-causing anomalies, including reconciling your numbers with a stakeholder's or customer's own analysis. Demonstrated experience supporting internal teams by managing a queue of data and reporting requests and prioritizing by impact and urgency. Comfortable conducting ad-hoc analysis and presenting findings to cross-functional teams Excellent communication skills and the ability to present complex data clearly to non-technical audiences, including customer-facing teams who will share your findings with customers. Nice to Haves: Familiarity with data transformation frameworks and approaches (e.g., dbt, materialized views, incremental models, data pipeline tools). Proficiency with the Python data analytics stack (Numpy, pandas, Jupyter, etc.). Expected for the Senior Data Analyst level. Experience using AI tools (e.g., Claude, coding agents, MCP) to automate analysis workflows or build internal tools. Understanding of fundamental ML concepts, familiarity with model evaluation metrics (precision and recall, false positive and false negative trade-offs). Background in fraud prevention, identity, device intelligence, or another domain where accuracy errors carry a real cost. Experience working directly with Customer Success, Sales, or Support teams in a B2B SaaS company. Technologies: Our stack: Clickhouse, DBT, Apache Superset (Preset), Prefect, Python and Jupyter, Claude Relevant technologies: Google BigQuery, Amazon Redshift, Snowflake, Apache Druid, Vertica, DataBricks, Apache Airflow, Dataform, Talend, Fivetran, Stitch, Luigi, Dagster, Tableau, Power BI, Looker, Metabase, Redash Compensation & Transparency At Fingerprint, we believe in pay transparency — it's part of how we operate as a distributed, remote-first team. Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management (LIM) Operations Tooling team builds the products that run the Leo network day to day. Our tools are used by the Network Operations Center, Call Leaders, and service teams across Networking, Commerce, and Satellite Operations to see the health of the network, catch problems before customers do, coordinate fast when something goes wrong, and automate the work that slows operators down. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production. Key job responsibilities Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and tools that power network operations and incident management for Amazon Leo. Build proactive health capabilities, including anomaly and trend detection, early warning features, and proactive investigation workflows that help operators act before customers are affected. Build alarm correlation and deduplication systems so responders see one problem instead of hundreds of alerts. Build NOC dashboards and operator workflows that bring health, customer impact, affected components, and ongoing events into one view. Build self-service tooling that lets service teams onboard and manage their own health signals, alarms, and runbooks. Automate runbook steps, data collection, and repetitive operational tasks so operators spend their time on judgment, not mechanics. Integrate with observability, telemetry, ticketing, paging, and communication systems across Amazon Leo, including the network observability platform. Apply automation, machine learning, and generative AI to triage, event summarization, timeline drafting, and correlation where it measurably improves outcomes. Design systems that stay available when the network they serve is degraded, since operators need these tools most during an outage. Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support. Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software. Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. A day in the life You might start the day with feedback from the NOC on a dashboard you shipped last week and fix a workflow that slowed operators down during an overnight event. Midday, you could be designing a correlation service that groups alarms from many services into a single event, or building the escalation engine that pages the right leader when an event has been open too long. In the afternoon you might pair with the product manager on a self-service onboarding flow, review code, and prototype an AI-drafted event summary for Call Leaders. Your work shows up every time an issue is caught earlier, resolved faster, or never happens at all. At Amazon Foundation Security Services (AFSS), our team is building out a renewed set of foundational access management capabilities for all of Amazon’s digital and physical resources. We are a fun, collaborative team, and we focus on empowering everyone on the team achieve their next goal. We are responsible for the protection of customer and corporate data, while being connected to all parts of Amazon's business and its massive worldwide service-oriented architecture. Whether you're passionate about building highly scalable and reliable systems in the cloud or a software developer who likes to solve interesting and complex business problems, AFSS is the place for you. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate foundational security services and access management systems. There is ample opportunity to innovate and deliver high impact outcomes. You will collaborate with the leadership team to drive key engineering and business decisions that will influence the Amazon developer experience. You will contribute to all parts of the software development and deployment lifecycle across the entire Amazon development community, including design, implementation, documentation, deployment and operations across multiple products. Successful candidates for this position will have strong software engineering fundamentals such as object-oriented design, algorithms, and data structures. They must possess strong verbal and written communication skills, be self-driven and deliver high results. They need to really enjoy working closely with their peers within a group of very talented engineers and builders. This position involves on-call responsibilities, typically for one week every two months. We don’t like getting paged in the middle of the night or on the weekend, so we work to ensure that our systems are fault tolerant. When we do get paged, we work together to resolve the root cause so that we don’t get paged for the same issue twice. Key job responsibilities • Collaborate with experienced cross-disciplinary Amazonians to conceive, design, and bring innovative products and services to market. • Design and build innovative technologies in a large distributed computing environment and help lead fundamental changes in the industry. • Create solutions to run predictions on distributed systems with exposure to innovative technologies at incredible scale and speed. • Build distributed storage, index, and query systems that are scalable, fault-tolerant, low cost, and easy to manage/use. • Design and code the right solutions starting with broadly defined problems. • Work in an agile environment to deliver high-quality software. A day in the life The challenges SDEs solve for at Amazon are big and influence millions of customers, sellers, and products around the world. We are looking for individuals who are passionate about creating new products, features, and services from scratch while managing ambiguity and the pace of a company where development cycles are measured in weeks, not years. About the team Diverse Experiences Amazon Security values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all of the qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying. Why Amazon Security? At Amazon, security is central to maintaining customer trust and delivering delightful customer experiences. Our organization is responsible for creating and maintaining a high bar for security across all of Amazon’s products and services. We offer talented security professionals the chance to accelerate their careers with opportunities to build experience in a wide variety of areas including cloud, devices, retail, entertainment, healthcare, operations, and physical stores. jobs.jd_excerpt: We prioritize applicants who apply directly on our site: https://emberline.com/careers About Emberline Emberline is an investment firm that buys and builds businesses in B2B services and software. We're operators at heart, not spectators. We work alongside company teams to build better products, sharpen how the work gets done and ship software customers are delighted to use. The role We're actively hiring software engineers for several openings across the Emberline portfolio of companies. These are earlier-career roles with guidance, mentorship and support. You'd join one of our portfolio companies and take on scoped work with technical direction and growing responsibility as your skills develop. You might build a feature customers have been asking for, improve a workflow that's harder than it should be, refactor existing code, or connect systems, APIs and data that should work together. For example, one company builds web and mobile software that helps first responders make sense of maps and live operational data during emergencies. That's one kind of work in the portfolio, not a background you need to bring. We ship on newer frameworks where they fit and keep looking for ways to automate the SDLC, from scoping and context through implementation, review, testing and release. We also help evolve the rails the whole company runs on: the systems, integrations and workflows behind the business. Where you stand out Correct, secure and usable software is the baseline. We look for people who stand out in one or more of these ways: You turn a scoped need into working software, connect systems, make messy data usable and keep the build the right size. Sometimes the fastest way to clarify a requirement is to put a working version in someone's hands. You care whether software holds up when data arrives late or wrong. You write tests that make change safe and check failure cases, not just the happy path, so verification keeps up with agents. You care about clear states, useful feedback and navigation that makes sense. You notice the screen that works but still feels unfinished, and agents may have brought out your inner designer. In high-stakes settings, delight means clarity under pressure, not decoration. Who you are We won't ask whether you use AI. That's like asking whether you use email. We're interested in how you build: You direct agents through real implementation work. You scope the task, give agents useful context, instruction files and skills, and let them cook. You inspect, debug and test the result, and catch when an agent is confidently wrong. You understand and verify what you ship. You can debug, change and explain it, test the behavior and failure cases that matter, and keep security and customer-data boundaries intact. Full-stack reach is preferred, and product- or design-oriented engineers are welcome when the building ability is real. You're curious and welcome feedback. You ask candid questions, raise blockers early and say plainly what you're unsure about. You incorporate feedback quickly and often. You take initiative and follow through. You get oriented in code you didn't write, move work forward without every step spelled out, and finish it through the team's review and release process. You keep upgrading how you build. Repeated work bothers you until you automate it away. You enjoy trying new agentic workflows on real projects and keeping what helps. We don't really care about your background. What matters is working software you can walk us through, and how you built it. How you'll work and grow You'll have an experienced engineer supporting you, reviewing your work, helping you scope it and talking through tradeoffs. Expect direct feedback on your code and your approach. Your work starts sized to that support and grows as you show what you can carry. You'll do meaningful engineering at a company whose customers depend on it. Emberline has its own support and software development teams and works closely with each company. Strong performers may have opportunities to take on broader roles, including at Emberline, with greater responsibility and financial upside. How to apply Apply here: https://emberline.com/careers Select Associate Engineer as the role you're applying for. We use one first-round application for all engineering hires, with written questions and a short voice response. You can save your progress and return to finish. We take the application seriously, and it's your best chance to stand out.

jobs.jd_excerpt:
Amazon Leo is Amazon's low Earth orbit satellite network, with a mission to deliver fast, reliable internet connectivity to customers beyond the reach of existing networks. From individual households to schools, hospitals, businesses, and government agencies, Amazon Leo will connect people and organizations operating in locations without reliable connectivity. The Leo NOC and Leo Incident Management (LIM) Operations Tooling team builds the products that run the Leo network day to day. Our tools are used by the Network Operations Center, Call Leaders, and service teams across Networking, Commerce, and Satellite Operations to see the health of the network, catch problems before customers do, coordinate fast when something goes wrong, and automate the work that slows operators down. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to design, build, and operate these tools. You will turn health signals and network telemetry into operator workflows and automation, proactive health and early warning features, NOC dashboards and runbook automation, alarm correlation and noise reduction, incident management and escalation tooling, and the post-event systems that feed every lesson back into better detection. You will work closely with the product manager, operators, and Call Leaders who use your tools every day, and you will own what you build from design through production. Export Control Requirement: Due to applicable export control laws and regulations, candidates must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e., current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, and operate scalable, highly available services and tools that power network operations and incident management for Amazon Leo. - Build proactive health capabilities, including anomaly and trend detection, early warning features, and proactive investigation workflows that help operators act before customers are affected. - Build alarm correlation and deduplication systems so responders see one problem instead of hundreds of alerts. - Build NOC dashboards and operator workflows that bring health, customer impact, affected components, and ongoing events into one view. - Build self-service tooling that lets service teams onboard and manage their own health signals, alarms, and runbooks. - Automate runbook steps, data collection, and repetitive operational tasks so operators spend their time on judgment, not mechanics. - Integrate with observability, telemetry, ticketing, paging, and communication systems across Amazon Leo, including the network observability platform. - Apply automation, machine learning, and generative AI to triage, event summarization, timeline drafting, and correlation where it measurably improves outcomes. - Design systems that stay available when the network they serve is degraded, since operators need these tools most during an outage. - Participate in the full software development lifecycle, including architecture, implementation, testing, deployment, operational readiness, and on-call support. - Mentor other engineers and contribute to a culture of high-quality, secure, and maintainable software. A day in the life You might start the day with feedback from the NOC on a dashboard you shipped last week and fix a workflow that slowed operators down during an overnight event. Midday, you could be designing a correlation service that groups alarms from many services into a single event, or building the escalation engine that pages the right leader when an event has been open too long. In the afternoon you might pair with the product manager on a self-service onboarding flow, review code, and prototype an AI-drafted event summary for Call Leaders. Your work shows up every time an issue is caught earlier, resolved faster, or never happens at all. About the team The Leo NOC and LIM Operations Tooling team builds the operational products that keep a global space and terrestrial telecom network healthy and its operations efficient. We sit next to the people who use our tools, the Network Operations Center and the Incident Management Team. We measure success by how much faster, quieter, and more automated operations become as the network scales toward and beyond general availability.

jobs.jd_excerpt: At Meta, we're building and operating one of the world's most dynamic and fast-paced networks, powering our global data centers and supporting cutting-edge technologies like AI, Generative AI, Recommendation engines, and the Metaverse. Our network infrastructure teams are responsible for developing, deploying, and operating this complex system, covering the entire network lifecycle from hardware development to operation. FBOSS is a software team in the Network Infrastructure group that powers the network devices Meta runs. FBOSS stands for Facebook Open Switching System - a software stack running on network switches across Meta's global network. We work on some of the most critical infrastructure challenges at Meta, including the networking switch platforms behind our AI clusters for large language models, recommendation systems, and the metaverse. This role is part of our FBOSS Platform SW team which works across every stage of a network switch: defining new switch requirements, hardware/software design, software development, bringing up current Linux kernels on our switch platforms, and supporting them in operation. Why this role, and why now: Our switching platforms have historically operated in facilities where physical access and the surrounding network are tightly controlled. We are now extending these platforms into environments that do not offer those guarantees - including backbone and other less-trusted deployment settings - where the platform itself has to carry security properties it previously inherited from its surroundings. This role exists to close that gap across platform, operating system, and data plane security. You will work in an Azure environment using Python, Databricks and Snowflake, partnering with business stakeholders, data engineers and AI engineers to take use cases from idea to evaluated, production ready models. This position can be based remotely anywhere in the United States. The client's preferred location is Alpharetta, Georgia. What You'll Do Key Responsibilities Partner with business and CDO stakeholders to translate AI, GenAI and Agentic AI use cases into well defined data science problems with measurable success criteria. Explore, profile and engineer features from large structured and unstructured datasets in Databricks and Snowflake. Build, train, tune and validate predictive, classification, forecasting, clustering and NLP models in Python. Design evaluation frameworks for GenAI and agentic solutions, including quality, groundedness, relevance, bias, safety and cost/performance metrics, plus A/B and offline testing. Prototype and assess LLM based approaches (prompting, retrieval augmented generation, embeddings, fine tuning candidates) and compare them against classical baselines. Collaborate with AI engineers and data engineers to hand off validated models and pipelines for productionization, and support monitoring for drift and performance degradation. Apply responsible AI practices: explainability, fairness testing, model documentation and alignment with CDO governance and risk standards. Communicate findings, trade offs and recommendations to technical and non technical audiences through clear analysis, visuals and written summaries. Contribute to reusable notebooks, feature sets and data science standards across the CDO. What You'll Bring: Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Computer Science, Data Science, Engineering or a related quantitative field; Master's or PhD preferred. 4+ years of professional experience as a Data Scientist delivering models into business use. Strong Python for data science (pandas, NumPy, scikit learn, and at least one of XGBoost/LightGBM, PyTorch or TensorFlow). Strong SQL and hands on experience with Snowflake for data exploration, feature creation and analysis. Hands on experience in Databricks (notebooks, Spark/PySpark, MLflow for experiment tracking). Experience working in Azure (e.g., Azure Data Lake, Azure Machine Learning or Azure OpenAI/AI Foundry exposure). Solid foundation in statistics and machine learning: hypothesis testing, regression, tree based models, feature engineering, cross validation and model evaluation. Working knowledge of GenAI concepts: LLMs, embeddings, prompt design, retrieval augmented generation and how to evaluate LLM output. Familiarity with Agentic AI concepts (tool use, multi step agents, orchestration) sufficient to define use cases and evaluation approaches. Ability to explain technical results clearly to business stakeholders and work in a cross functional team. Experience with Git and collaborative development practices. Preferred Qualifications Prior experience in a Chief Data Office, enterprise data governance or regulated industry setting (financial services, healthcare, insurance). Hands on LLM work with Azure OpenAI, including RAG prototypes and evaluation tooling (e.g., MLflow evaluation, Ragas or similar). Familiarity with agent frameworks (LangChain, LangGraph, Semantic Kernel, AutoGen) from an experimentation or evaluation standpoint. Experience with Snowflake Cortex or Snowpark, and Databricks Mosaic AI, Feature Store or Unity Catalog. NLP experience: text classification, entity extraction, topic modeling or semantic search. Time series forecasting, causal inference or experimentation (A/B testing) experience. Knowledge of responsible AI, model risk management and explainability techniques (SHAP, LIME). Data visualization skills (Power BI, Streamlit or similar). Relevant certifications (e.g., Azure Data Scientist Associate, Databricks Machine Learning Associate/Professional, SnowPro). #DICE Other Information: CGI is required by law in some jurisdictions to include a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role. Come shape the future with us.</p></div><p><strong>SPACE SYSTEMS</strong></p> <p>At Rocket Lab, we’re not just launching rockets — we're building the future of space. jobs.jd_excerpt: About The Role The role turns messy, high-volume data into models that drive core product and business decisions — from exploratory analysis and experimentation to statistical models running in production. Working within a cross-functional team of ML engineers, data engineers, and product stakeholders, this person owns the full analytical lifecycle: framing the problem, designing experiments, building models in Python and SQL, and shipping results that leadership actually acts on. Key Responsibilities Design and execute A/B tests and quasi-experimental analyses (diff-in-diff, synthetic control, CUPED) to measure causal impact of product changes Build predictive models — classification, forecasting, churn/propensity — in Python using scikit-learn, XGBoost, or PyTorch, with production deployment in mind Write complex SQL against large-scale data warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, or Databricks) and partner with data engineers on pipeline design in dbt and Airflow Develop and maintain dashboards and self-serve analytics in Tableau, Looker, or Plotly that leadership uses for weekly decision-making Translate ambiguous business questions into rigorous analytical frameworks, and communicate findings clearly to both technical and executive audiences Conduct exploratory analysis on user behavior, product funnels, and operational data to identify growth and efficiency opportunities Uphold statistical rigor across the team — experiment design reviews, metric definitions, and documentation of methodology What We Are Looking For 3–6 years of experience in data science, applied analytics, or machine learning, ideally in a product-led technology company Expert-level SQL and strong Python (pandas, NumPy, scikit-learn); comfort working with datasets at petabyte scale Hands-on experience designing and analyzing A/B tests, including power analysis, sequential testing, and guarding against common pitfalls like interference and novelty effects Track record of shipping at least one model or analytical product end-to-end — from stakeholder alignment to production deployment Experience with cloud data platforms (Snowflake, Databricks, BigQuery) and modern workflow tooling (Airflow, dbt, Git) Master's degree in statistics, computer science, economics, math, or a related quantitative field (or equivalent industry experience) Bonus: experience with causal inference libraries (DoWhy, EconML), big data tooling (PySpark), LLM-assisted analytics, or publishing applied research
