jobs.jd_excerpt: Rezolute is a late-stage rare disease biopharmaceutical company focused on developing transformative therapies for patients living with severe metabolic and endocrine disorders. Our mission is to bring hope and meaningful solutions to patients and families affected by rare and difficult-to-treat diseases through scientific innovation, collaboration, and integrity. Rezolute’s lead investigational therapy, RZ358 (ersodetug), is a fully human monoclonal antibody in late-stage clinical development for the treatment of hypoglycemia due to congenital and acquired forms of hyperinsulinism (HI). As Rezolute expands its medical and scientific focus into tumor-related hyperinsulinism (tumor HI), most commonly related to pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (insulinomas) or paraneoplastic hypoglycemia (NICTH), the company is committed to advancing novel therapeutic strategies that address this rare and complex form of hypoglycemia associated with insulin-secreting tumors and related neuro-oncology disorders. More information can be found at rezolutebio.com Position Summary Rezolute is seeking a Data Analyst II to turn complex data into actionable insights supporting commercial planning, medical affairs, and business decision-making. This hands-on role combines data management, coding, analysis, and visualization to help teams better understand patient populations, healthcare providers, treatment patterns, and market opportunities. The Data Analyst II will use AWS, Snowflake, SQL, and Python or R to integrate data, automate analytical workflows, and develop reliable datasets and reporting solutions. Working closely with business stakeholders, this individual will translate questions into structured analyses and communicate findings through clear visualizations, reports, and presentations. The ideal candidate brings strong technical skills, sound analytical judgment, and a collaborative, self-directed approach. Experience with healthcare claims or other pharmaceutical industry data is a plus. Key Responsibilities Acquire, clean, integrate, and manage healthcare and business data using AWS, Snowflake, SQL, and Python or R. Build, deploy, and maintain reusable data pipelines, analytical datasets, and scheduled code in AWS and Snowflake. Develop a strong working knowledge of healthcare data and the biopharmaceutical industry, including how claims, provider, and market data reflect patient care and business activity. Conduct exploratory and statistical analyses to identify trends, answer business questions, and generate actionable insights. Apply statistical and machine learning methods, where appropriate, to support patient identification, segmentation, and prioritization, with clear documentation of methods, validation, and limitations. Support analyses of patient populations, healthcare providers and organizations, treatment patterns, market dynamics, and field-team activity. Develop dashboards, reports, and visualizations in Power BI, Tableau, Python, or comparable tools. Automate recurring data preparation, quality checks, and reporting processes to reduce manual effort. Qualifications Bachelor's degree with a minimum of 3 years' experience in a quantitative or technical field, such as statistics, mathematics, economics, computer science, or engineering, or equivalent practical experience. Relevant professional experience in data analytics, data management, analytics engineering, or a related field. Hands-on experience with AWS and Snowflake for data storage, querying, transformation, or analytical workflows. Strong SQL skills and proficiency in Python or R for data manipulation, analysis, and automation. Experience cleaning, combining, and analyzing large or complex datasets. jobs.jd_excerpt: You are not just building reports or moving data. You are turning reliable data into insights that help the business act. The Analytics Engineering role combines data engineering and data analysis to build reliable pipelines, maintain trusted datasets, and deliver reporting and insights for a multi-location car wash network. This hands-on role connects enterprise systems and translates operational, customer, membership, sales, and financial data into practical insights. Working with technology and business partners across Operations, Finance, Marketing, and HR, this role supports both the data foundation and the analysis built on it—from source integration and transformation to dashboards, business questions, and recurring reporting. At this level, success is measured by dependable data pipelines, accurate and consistent reporting, fewer manual reporting steps, and insights that business partners can understand and use. What You’ll Do Data Engineering & Integration Build, maintain, and troubleshoot data pipelines that bring together POS, membership, CRM, ERP, HRIS, and other enterprise data sources. Develop SQL transformations and reusable data models that support operational, customer, and financial analysis. Use APIs, file-based integrations, and ETL/ELT processes to move data reliably between source systems and reporting platforms. Monitor pipeline health, investigate failures, and document dependencies, refresh schedules, and recovery procedures. Analytics & Business Insights Partner with business teams to clarify questions, define reporting requirements, and translate needs into actionable analysis. Analyze site performance, membership trends, customer retention, pricing, and sales to identify patterns and opportunities. Build and maintain dashboards, recurring reports, and self-service datasets with clear metric definitions. Explain findings, assumptions, and data limitations in practical terms for nontechnical stakeholders. Data Quality, Governance & Documentation Validate source data, reconcile reporting outputs, and investigate discrepancies with system owners and business partners. Create automated quality checks for completeness, accuracy, consistency, and freshness. Maintain documentation for data models, transformations, source mappings, metric definitions, and reporting logic. Follow established access controls, data handling standards, and governance practices when working with sensitive information. Automation & Cross-Functional Partnership Automate repeatable reporting and data preparation tasks to reduce manual work and improve consistency. Support system implementations and acquisition integrations through data mapping, migration validation, and reporting continuity. Use version control, testing, and change documentation to make data solutions maintainable and dependable. Balance engineering maintenance and analysis requests with technology and business partners, communicating priorities, dependencies, and delivery expectations. Where you Lead, Shape & Escalate Lead Assigned data pipelines, transformations, data quality checks, dashboards, recurring reporting, technical documentation, and analytical deliverables. Shape Metric definitions, reusable data models, reporting requirements, automation opportunities, self-service analytics, and improvements to data reliability and usability. Escalate Source-system limitations, unresolved data discrepancies, pipeline failures, sensitive-data access concerns, conflicting metric definitions, and delivery dependencies that could affect reporting accuracy or business decisions. What We’re Looking For We are looking for a hands-on data professional who can build dependable data solutions and explain what the numbers mean for the business. Practical experience in data analysis, data engineering, business intelligence, or a blended role spanning these disciplines. Strong SQL skills, including querying, joining, transforming, validating, and troubleshooting data across multiple sources. Experience building and maintaining ETL/ELT pipelines, relational data models, and datasets in a cloud data warehouse or comparable environment. Proficiency with a scripting language such as Python for data preparation, integration, automation, and quality checks. Experience developing dashboards and reports in a business intelligence platform and translating business questions into clear visualizations. Working knowledge of APIs, data integration patterns, version control, testing, and technical documentation. Ability to investigate data issues, reconcile conflicting results, and communicate findings and limitations clearly. Ability to manage competing priorities and collaborate with technical teams and nontechnical business partners. Experience with multi-site, consumer-facing, retail, service, or subscription-based businesses is preferred. Familiarity with POS, membership, CRM, ERP, HRIS, or operational data is a plus. The best data professionals do more than deliver a dataset or dashboard. They connect trustworthy data with the decisions that move the business forward. Base Pay Range $90,000.00 - $175,000.00

jobs.jd_excerpt: Description The AWS Analytics Engineering (AAE) organization is the analytics backbone of AWS. We build and operate the data platform that powers business decisions across more than 250 AWS services. Every insight surfaced to AWS product leadership, from service adoption trends to revenue drivers, flows through systems our team designs, builds, and maintains. We operate at massive scale, processing petabytes of data daily through thousands of jobs spanning transformations, reporting queries, ingestions, and infrastructure management scripts. Our engineers work directly with source systems to procure data, convert it into structured formats, build large-scale processing pipelines, design analytical data models, and maintain infrastructure with the highest security and compliance standards. We are seeking a Data Engineer II to join our team. You will own data pipelines and analytical models within one or more data domains, improve the quality and accessibility of high-value datasets, and contribute to architectural improvements that support how AWS leaders make decisions. You will partner with service teams across AWS to clarify data requirements, implement data contracts and ingestion flows, and deliver scalable analytical datasets for customers across the organization. The ideal candidate is an experienced data engineer who independently delivers reliable solutions to difficult data problems and seeks direction when broader architectural decisions require it. You have strong SQL, ETL, data modeling, and programming skills, with experience using cloud-based data services such as AWS EMR, Glue, Redshift, and Lambda. Experience applying AI/ML technologies, including LLMs and agentic workflows, to data engineering use cases is valuable. You are comfortable working through loosely defined requirements, collaborating with technical and business partners, and building secure, maintainable data solutions at AWS scale. Key job responsibilities Design, build, and optimize logical data models and data pipelines for difficult datasets in the team's area. Translate loosely defined business requirements into secure, testable, maintainable, and efficient data solutions. Own the quality and operational health of assigned datasets and pipelines. Establish monitoring, alarming, runbooks, data validation, and SLA tracking, and participate in the team's on-call rotation. Contribute to data architecture and design decisions for the solutions you own. Apply established patterns and make sound trade-offs among delivery speed, scalability, maintainability, security, and cost. Build and operate infrastructure for assigned data solutions using automation and team standards. Anticipate access and processing needs, troubleshoot failures, and remove recurring operational bottlenecks. Partner with AWS service teams and analytics customers to clarify requirements, define data contracts, resolve data quality issues, and improve self-service access to trusted datasets. Own projects or substantial project components from design through launch and ongoing operations. Identify dependencies and risks, coordinate with peers and partner teams, and escalate when broader alignment or architectural guidance is needed. Apply data engineering best practices for code quality, testing, documentation, naming, dependency management, data certification, security, and auditability. Participate in code reviews and design discussions, provide constructive technical feedback, share knowledge, and begin mentoring less-experienced engineers. Identify limitations in existing data solutions and implement or propose improvements. Contribute to reusable patterns and larger architectural initiatives led by senior engineers. Explore and apply AI/ML technologies, including LLMs and agentic workflows, to improve data discovery, pipeline development, operational support, and analytics productivity. jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><h3 id="about-self-financial" data-lfile-container="92a8cfe3-e7d5-4ff0-b516-f7f6b8f35540" data-pm-slice="1 1 []">About Self Financial</h3> <p>Self Financial is a venture-backed, high-growth FinTech company with a mission to increase economic inclusion and financial resilience by empowering people to build credit and build savings.</p> <p>We challenge the status quo of the credit industry by giving people accessible tools to take control of their credit, with a focus on the 100 million+ Americans who have no or low credit. We're looking for people who share our passion, tackle challenges, find solutions, and make the financial space better for the communities we serve.</p></div><h3><strong>Title</strong></h3> <p>Associate Software Engineer</p> <h3><strong>Team </strong></h3> <p><strong>Credit Builder Account (CBA) </strong>is a product team, much like our card team. CBA&nbsp;is a way to credit. It is a loan in a bank-held Certificate of Deposit (CD) that members can pay off. Each payment gets reported to all three credit bureaus. The CBA team builds and operates the systems supporting the product, including the services, APIs, jobs, mobile webs and web platforms.</p> <p><strong>Location:</strong> Austin, TX</p> <p><strong>Work Arrangement:</strong> Austin – Hybrid</p> <h3><strong>About the Role</strong></h3> <p>You’ll join CBA early in your career and learn how a regulated fintech product is built, shipped, and maintained. You’ll implement, develop, and test software, collaborating with senior engineers to understand project requirements and complete assigned tasks. You’ll also work alongside product managers, QA, and DevOps, and use AI tools like Claude every day to write code and move the product forward.</p> <p><strong>What you’ll do:</strong></p> <ul> <li>Build new features and enhancements for the Credit Builder Account, and feel comfortable raising questions when something is unclear.</li> <li>Ship functional, secure Python code, REST APIs, and integrations with in-house and third-party services and SQL databases, collaborating through Git (branches, pull requests, code reviews).</li> <li>Debug and resolve issues by digging in and understanding the root cause, not just patching the symptom.</li> <li>Use good judgment: ask questions, weigh tradeoffs, flag risks, and keep our work aligned with compliance requirements as a regulated fintech.</li> <li>Own what you ship. Use Claude and other AI tools to move faster, but review, understand, and stand behind every line of code.</li> <li>Partner with product managers, QA, DevOps, and teams across the company to deliver on product goals.</li> <li>Keep growing: take feedback from code reviews in stride, learn from mistakes, and stretch into harder problems over time.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What You Bring</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Associates, Bachelors, or Masters in Computer Science or a related field, or equivalent internship, project, or hands-on experience.</li> <li>Proficiency in Python, with a solid grasp of core data structures and algorithms (you can explain why one approach is better than another).</li> <li>Working knowledge of REST APIs.</li> <li>Experience with SQL databases.</li> <li>Familiarity with Git and collaborative development workflows.</li> <li>Understanding of unit testing and how to apply it.</li> <li>Clear communication and a willingness to ask questions, take feedback, and learn quickly.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>What Separates You</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Relevant software engineering internships or project work.</li> <li>Hands-on experience with AWS or another cloud provider.</li> <li>Understanding of CI/CD and how code actually gets deployed, including the broader software development life cycle.</li> <li>Real exposure to AI-assisted development (such as Claude) in school, internships, or personal projects.</li> </ul> <h3 id="pay-range-2">Salary Pay Range</h3> <p>$90,000 – $120,000 annually. Our AI research lab discovers and develops methods to recognize patterns and predict outcomes across complex, multi-modal clinical data. jobs.jd_excerpt: <div class="content-intro"><h1>Who We Are:</h1> <p>Power Digital is an AI-Native Growth Firm built at the intersection of world-class talent and proprietary technology. We help leading and emerging brands grow by combining deep vertical expertise, strategic thinking, and enterprise intelligence to drive measurable business outcomes.</p> <p>For more than a decade, we have built our business around one belief: the best technology makes great people better. Our teams of strategists, creatives, analysts, and technologists use Omega, our AI operating system, to surface opportunities faster, investigate what is driving performance, and execute approved work with greater speed and precision. Behind Omega is Iris, our proprietary intelligence layer, built on years of real performance data, strategic frameworks, testing, and learnings from across our client portfolio. AI expands the capacity of our people to think, create, solve harder problems, and make better decisions. Human judgment, creativity, and accountability remain central to how we work.&nbsp;</p> <p>As a people-first firm, we value diversity in backgrounds and experiences. We strongly believe our people and culture are key to our success. We partner closely with our clients as an extension of their teams, working across strategy, execution, and measurement to identify what is truly blocking growth and determine what to do next. Our culture is built on people who are curious, ambitious, accountable, and committed to delivering meaningful results for our clients and for one another.</p> <p>At Power Digital, we believe the future belongs to teams that combine the best talent with the best technology. We are building that future today.</p></div><p><strong>***Proficiency in spoken and written English at an advanced level is required for this role.</strong></p> <p><strong>A day in the life:</strong></p> <p>You'll sit on the fusepoint Marketing Science Team and own the data behind Power Digital's measurement products: Media Mix Modeling (MMM) and incrementality testing (Matched Market Testing, MMT). Our measurement tools are used by internal and external teams to read model results, plan budgets, pick test markets and report on incrementality tests. Your job is to make sure the data needed for measurement analysis is clean, reconciled and ready for modeling, so the analysts and data scientists spend their time on modeling, not cleanup.</p> <p>You'll work closely with the Data Team to support, maintain, and engineer data sources related to measurement and marketing metrics.&nbsp;</p> <p><strong>Key Responsibilities:</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Own the MMM data layer in Snowflake. </strong>Build and maintain model-ready daily and weekly marts for each client that combine paid media (spend, impressions, clicks by channel and campaign), ecommerce revenue and orders (new vs. returning, gross and net, refunds, discounts), site and email/SMS data from GA4, and any non-media drivers. Every mart has consistent channel groupings, currencies and timezones.</li> <li><strong>Own the MMT geo data layer. </strong>Build geo-level media and sales tables at DMA (or Comscore), state and zip level for every major platform (Meta, Google, TikTok, Pinterest, Amazon, Microsoft, Programmatic, etc.) and for CMS/CRM/Amazon/Retail Datsets, with standard market names that line up across sources. These tables feed automated market selection, pre-period validation, synthetic control models and test readouts.</li> <li><strong>Build and automate a data quality process</strong>. Turn the checks we currently run manually into automated Snowflake/dbt tests and alerts: date gaps, zero-spend or zero-revenue days, cost without impressions (and the reverse), duplicated or unmatched markets, outlier spikes, restatement drift and source freshness. Problems should be flagged before a model is trained or a test is read out.</li> <li><strong>Own and maintain model logs and exported model outputs </strong>(contributions, response curves, adstock, optimization results) well structured, versioned and easy to query.</li> <li><strong>Support onboarding of new measurement clients. </strong>Own and maintain a repeatable, mostly automated process: map their data feeds, check history depth and quality, and flag gaps before modeling starts.</li> <li><strong>Handle client-specific data needs as they come up. </strong>You are not responsible for client workflow, but you may need to jump in to assist the team as things come up.. Write client-specific overrides, channel mappings and marts when a client needs them, and decide whether each piece of logic belongs in the shared core or in the client's own layer.</li> <li>Use AI coding tools to work faster (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, Hex's AI agent), and document the patterns that work so the team adopts them.</li> </ul> <p><strong>Role Requirements:</strong></p> <ul> <li>3+ years in data or analytics engineering, including 1+ year owning a production dbt project of meaningful size.</li> <li>Advanced SQL and Python, with production-grade pipeline code.</li> <li>Deep dbt expertise: incremental models vs. full refreshes, Jinja and macros, tests, snapshots, source freshness, exposures, and keeping a large DAG under control.</li> <li>Strong Snowflake skills: semi-structured/VARIANT data, dynamic per-client queries, query and cost tuning, permissions across separate client databases.</li> <li>Hands-on marketing and ecommerce data experience: ad-platform APIs, UTMs, attribution windows, platform-reported v

jobs.jd_excerpt: Overview Join the Xanterra Travel Collection team: Xanterra Travel Collection is a premier group of travel and leisure businesses with a focus on sustainability and exceptional service. Headquartered in Greenwood Village, Colorado, we operate iconic properties and services in stunning locations worldwide, including lodging, food and beverage, Windstar Cruises, short-line railroads, and adventure travel. We are dedicated to creating unforgettable experiences for our guests and providing transformative career opportunities for our team members. Job Summary: The Analytics Engineer joins a small but mighty Data & Analytics team responsible for the data products and reporting used across Xanterra's operations, finance, sales, and revenue management teams. This is a hands-on role for someone who enjoys working across the analytics stack rather than specializing in only one area. Approximately 60% of the role focuses on Power BI semantic models, measures, reporting, and dashboards, with the remaining 40% focused on the Snowflake and dbt data models that support them. You'll work across the full lifecycle, from understanding a business question to building the underlying data model and delivering the final reporting solution. The core platform is already established, so this role is focused on extending and improving the existing environment rather than building a new data platform from scratch. The team works with Snowflake, dbt, Power BI, and GitHub within a layered bronze, silver, and gold architecture. This is a strong fit for someone who likes owning their work from data model through final reporting and seeing how it is used by the business. You'll join a small team with an established modern data platform and have the opportunity to work with data across Xanterra's diverse portfolio of travel and hospitality businesses. This position reports to the Director, Data & Analytics and works onsite five days per week in Greenwood Village, Colorado. Candidates must currently reside within commuting distance of the Denver metropolitan area. Relocation assistance is not available. Responsibilities Build and maintain Power BI semantic models, including relationships, DAX measures, row-level security, and the reporting built on top of them. Develop SQL and dbt models in Snowflake using the team's established data architecture and development standards. Partner directly with business teams to understand reporting and analytics needs and translate them into reliable data products. Test and validate data products by reviewing record counts, keys, business rules, and reported figures against source systems. Create and maintain consistent metric and measure definitions so business users are working from consistent data across reports. Troubleshoot data and reporting issues, identify root causes, and communicate findings and resolutions clearly to business partners. Document data models, metrics, definitions, and key logic so both technical and business users can understand what the data represents. Participate in sprint planning, peer and code reviews, demonstrations, and retrospectives, and monitor assigned data processes for issues requiring resolution or escalation. Use approved AI-assisted development tools where appropriate, reviewing and validating generated work before release. Qualifications 3+ years of professional experience in analytics engineering, business intelligence, data analytics, or a related data-focused role. Bachelor's degree in a related field, or an equivalent combination of education and relevant experience. Strong SQL skills and experience working with data in a cloud-based environment. Hands-on Power BI experience, including data modeling and DAX measures. Working knowledge of data warehousing and dimensional modeling concepts. Ability to troubleshoot data issues, validate accuracy, and clearly communicate findings to both technical and nontechnical partners. Preferred Qualifications: Experience with Snowflake, dbt, GitHub, or similar modern data and development tools. Experience working with layered data architecture or automated data testing. Experience supporting hospitality, travel, retail, or another operations-focused business. Compensation: The salary range is $100,000 - $115,000 depending on experience. Benefits: For full-time employees, Xanterra offers a comprehensive benefits package including: Medical, Dental & Vision; HSA & FSA; Life & Disability; Accident, Hospital & Critical Illness; Pet Insurance; PTO and paid Holidays; 401(k) with Company Match; Employee Assistance Plan; Education Assistance; RTD-Denver transit pass for in-office employees, and Employee Discounts & Travel Deals. Xanterra Travel Collection is committed to a diverse and inclusive workplace. We are an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, genetic information, protected veteran status, or any other legally protected status.

We believe it is always Day 1, and we keep improving the service and adding new capabilities. DynamoDB is a serverless, fully managed database. It delivers consistent single-digit millisecond performance at any scale, with no servers to provision, no maintenance windows, and no downtime. Customers can create a table and scale it automatically to their most demanding workloads without having to plan capacity. During Prime Day 2026, DynamoDB handled more than 59 trillion requests over four days. It peaked at 192 million requests per second while keeping single-digit millisecond response times. The Capacity & Customer Entitlement (CCE) team builds the systems behind this. We decide how much throughput and storage each customer gets and enforce quotas and limits fairly. We also keep DynamoDB's global fleet ahead of demand. When our systems do their job, customers grow without thinking about capacity, and DynamoDB runs efficiently at any scale. Managing capacity for one of the largest databases in the world is a hard distributed systems problem. Our systems forecast demand across every AWS Region, plan and place capacity across the fleet, and manage the limits and entitlements that decide how far each customer can scale. We prepare DynamoDB for major events such as Prime Day and new Region launches, so capacity is in place well before customers need it. We are building fully automated capacity management from the ground up. It is a greenfield opportunity to design systems that detect, predict, and act on their own. Engineers on this team solve problems where accuracy, scale, and cost all matter at the same time, and their work shapes how customers experience DynamoDB. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.</p></div><h2>About the Team</h2> <p>The Imaging team builds and fields state-of-the-art camera and sensor systems deployed to solve real security challenges for the United States and its allies. We work across the full stack, from bare-metal hardware and firmware to networked services and cloud integrations, and we own our systems all the way through to the field. When something breaks in a deployed environment, we fix it.</p> <h2 id="MissionSoftwareEngineer-AbouttheRole">About the Role</h2> <p>We're looking for a Mission Software Engineer to join the Imaging Interfaces team. This is not a pure product development role. You will spend meaningful time keeping fielded systems alive, triaging issues across the full stack, and serving as a technical representative for our products in integrations with external teams and customers.<br><br>The work is varied and sometimes ambiguous. You might spend a morning extending a gRPC service, an afternoon diagnosing a time sync issue on a deployed device over the phone with a field operator, and a week traveling to support a customer integration. You'll need to be comfortable with that range--and ideally energized by it.<br><br>If you want to own your software end-to-end in a fast-moving environment where the stakes are real, this role is built for you.</p> <h2 id="MissionSoftwareEngineer-WhatYou'llDo">What You'll Do</h2> <p><strong>Own fielded system success.</strong> You are responsible for the health and uptime of deployed imaging systems. These services need to be reliable, observable, and maintainable by engineers who didn't write them.<br><br><strong>Support field operations.</strong> You'll work directly with field operators and non-technical users to diagnose and resolve issues on deployed hardware. Clear communication under pressure is part of the job.<br><br><strong>Represent the team externally.</strong> You'll serve as a subject matter expert in integrations with other products and teams; sometimes remotely, sometimes on-site. You don't need to know everything, but you need to be able to speak credibly across the full system stack and know what you don't know.<br><br><strong>Maintain end-to-end system understanding.</strong> Our devices sit at the intersection of hardware, firmware, networking, and software. You'll develop broad fluency across that stack over time, and apply it to optimize how our services interact and degrade gracefully when components fail.<br><br><strong>Collaborate across teams.</strong> You'll plan, build, and test complex functionality alongside firmware, hardware, and platform engineers. You'll need to be effective working across team and organizational boundaries.<br><br>Travel expected approximately 25% of the time for field testing and customer integrations.</p> <h2 id="MissionSoftwareEngineer-WhatWe'reLookingFor">What We're Looking For</h2> <h2 id="MissionSoftwareEngineer-Required">Required</h2> <ul> <li data-uuid="9a179e18-409e-44d3-997e-cd9e8156dfcc"><strong>3+ years of software development with meaningful production ownership:</strong>&nbsp;not just shipping features, but owning systems after they ship (their health, uptime, and behavior once they are in users' hands).</li> <li data-uuid="245897f6-d060-433d-91b5-808dcf1ade9e"><strong>Deep proficiency in at least one of C++, TypeScript(node.js/React), or Python, and the ability to work effectively across the stack boundary in a second language</strong>&nbsp;(reading, debugging, and modifying code outside your primary). jobs.jd_excerpt: About Ema Ema builds AI Employees for HR, IT and Finance. Our AI Employees take on the busy work across the employee experience, from recruiting, onboarding and benefits to IT support, invoice processing and payroll, so people can spend their time on work that needs them. Founded by former executives from Google, Coinbase, Flipkart, and Okta, our team includes engineers from premier tech companies and graduates of Stanford, MIT, UC Berkeley, CMU, and IITs. We are backed by industry leading investors including Accel, Naspers/Prosus, Creaegis, Section32, and angels like Sheryl Sandberg and Dustin Moskovitz. Headquartered in Silicon Valley and with offices in London, Bangalore and Vancouver, Ema is at the frontier of what Agentic AI can do in production. We ship real systems that run real business processes at scale. Who You Are We're looking for innovative and passionate Machine Learning Engineers to join our team. You are someone who loves solving complex problems, enjoys the challenges of working with huge data sets, and has a knack for turning theoretical concepts into practical, scalable solutions. You are a strong team player but also thrive in autonomous environments where your ideas can make a significant impact. You love utilizing machine learning techniques to push the boundaries of what is possible within the realm of Natural Language Processing, Information Retrieval and related spaces. Most importantly, you are excited to be part of a mission-oriented high-growth startup that can create a lasting impact. You Will Conceptualize, develop, and deploy machine learning models that underpin our NLP, retrieval, ranking, reasoning, dialog and code-generation systems. Implement advanced machine learning algorithms, such as Transformer-based models, reinforcement learning, ensemble learning, and agent-based systems to continually improve the performance of our AI systems. Process and analyze large, complex datasets (structured, semi-structured, and unstructured), and use your findings to inform the development of our models. Work across the complete lifecycle of ML model development, including problem definition, data exploration, feature engineering, model training, validation, and deployment. Implement A/B testing and other statistical methods to validate the effectiveness of models. Ensure the integrity and robustness of ML solutions by developing automated testing and validation processes. Clearly communicate the technical workings and benefits of ML models to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, facilitating understanding and adoption. Minimum Qualifications A Master’s degree or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Machine Learning, or a related quantitative field. At least 2 years of industry experience in building and deploying production-level machine learning models. Deep understanding and practical experience with NLP techniques and frameworks, including training and inference of large language models. Deep understanding of any of retrieval, ranking, reinforcement learning, and agent-based systems and experience in how to build them for large systems. Proficiency in Python and experience with ML libraries such as TensorFlow or PyTorch. Ideally, You'd Have Excellent skills in data processing (SQL, ETL, data warehousing) and experience working with large-scale data systems. Experience with machine learning model lifecycle management tools, and an understanding of MLOps principles and best practices. Familiarity with cloud platforms like GCP or Azure. Familiarity with the latest industry and academic trends in machine learning and AI, and the ability to apply this knowledge to practical projects. Good understanding of software development principles, data structures, and algorithms. Excellent problem-solving skills, attention to detail, and a strong capacity for logical thinking. The ability to work collaboratively in an extremely fast-paced, startup environment. For California Based Candidates The standard base salary for this position is $160,000 to $220,000 annually. Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for variable compensation, equity, and benefits. jobs.jd_excerpt: 🚀 Join the Future of Commerce with Whatnot! Whatnot is the largest live shopping platform in North America and Europe to buy, sell, and discover the things you love. Whether it's trading cards, fashion, electronics, or live plants, our sellers are building real businesses across hundreds of categories. We're building live commerce at a scale that's never been done in the West, and there's no playbook to copy. The people here are shaping how an entirely new industry develops. As a remote co-located team, we're inspired by our values and anchored in hubs across the US, UK, Ireland, Poland, Germany, and Australia. We move fast, stay close to our users, and focus on the work that drives the most impact. We're one of the fastest growing marketplaces and were recently named the #1 Best Startup Employer in America by Forbes. Check out the latest Whatnot updates on our news and engineering blogs and join us as we enable anyone to turn their passion into a business and bring people together through commerce. 💻 Role We're looking for entrepreneurial software engineers who thrive on ambiguous, 0-to-1 work. You’ll design and deploy both traditional ML models and infrastructure (contextual bandits to manage ad spend, shipment ETA predictions) and LLM-powered systems (RAG pipelines, human-in-the-loop evaluation frameworks) to address the business’s most pressing problems. Your job will change every ~12 months as we hand off stable products and pivot to address the business’s next big need. Strong applicants display exceptional business judgement and are equally comfortable contributing to production infrastructure and training the models that run on it. They build for the long term while finding ways to aggressively pull forward business impact. What You'll Do Develop and deploy new both production machine learning algorithms and core infrastructure to enrich the buyer and seller experience. Contribute to and set direction across the entire machine learning development process: opportunity sizing, feature engineering, model training, evaluation, load testing, deployment, and alerting. Design and implement supporting software infrastructure to unblock your work: streaming pipelines, async worker queues, event enrichment infrastructure, continuous training loops, model monitoring systems, LLM tool access controls, and dynamic agent evaluation framework to give just a few examples Define project roadmaps that deliver value quickly while building towards scalable, extensible long-term systems Bridge research and production: take an experimental idea and harden it into a scalable, well-tested, monitored system. Communicate tradeoffs and findings clearly to product and leadership. We offer flexibility to work from home or from one of our global office hubs, and we value in-person time for planning, problem-solving, and connection. Team members in this role must live within commuting distance of our Seattle or San Francisco hub. 👋 You Curious about who thrives at Whatnot? We've found that low ego, a growth mindset, and leaning into action and high impact goes a long way here. As our next Software Engineer, Core Machine Learning you should have 4+ years of professional experience, plus: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, or a related technical field, or equivalent work experience. 2+ years of software engineering experience building and maintaining production systems at consumer scale. 2+ years of hands-on experience training and deploying traditional ML models in production (e.g. classification, ranking, or regression models using PyTorch, LightGBM, or scikit-learn) Ability to work autonomously and drive initiatives across multiple product areas and communicate findings with leadership and product teams. Experience with operational, search, and key-value databases such as PostgreSQL, DynamoDB, Elasticsearch, Redis. Firm grasp of visualization tools for monitoring and logging e.g. DataDog, Grafana. Familiarity with cloud computing platforms and managed services such as AWS Kubernetes, Sagemaker, Lambda, Kinesis, S3, EC2, EKS/ECS, Apache Kafka, Flink. Professionalism around collaborating in a remote working environment and well tested, reproducible work. Exceptional documentation and communication skills. 💰Compensation For US-based applicants: $180,000 - $300,000/year + benefits + stock options The salary range may be inclusive of several levels that would be applicable to the position. Final salary will be based on a number of factors including, level, relevant prior experience, skills and expertise. This range is only inclusive of base salary, not benefits (more details below) or equity in the form of stock options. 🎁 Benefits Generous Holiday and Time off Policy Health Insurance options including Medical, Dental, Vision Work From Home Support Home office setup allowance Monthly allowance for cell phone and internet Care benefits Monthly allowance for wellness Annual allowance towards Childcare Lifetime benefit for family planning, such as adoption or fertility expenses Retirement; 401k offering for Traditional and Roth accounts in the US (employer match up to 4% of base salary) and Pension plans internationally Monthly allowance to dogfood the app All Whatnauts are expected to develop a deep understanding of our product. We're passionate about building the best user experience, and all employees are expected to use Whatnot as both a buyer and a seller as part of their job (our dogfooding budget makes this fun and easy!). Parental Leave 16 weeks of paid parental leave + one month gradual return to work *company leave allowances run concurrently with country leave requirements which take precedence. Please note: Whatnot will only contact you through official @whatnot.com email addresses. If you see an email impersonating a Whatnot recruiter, please disregard and report it as spam. 💛 EOE Whatnot is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. We value diversity, and we do not

jobs.jd_excerpt:
Have you ever wondered what it takes to build the software systems that turn a rack of AI accelerators from inert silicon into a system a customer can run workloads on? Do you want deep ownership of a service that every one of those systems depends on to boot, run, and stay healthy? **Who are we?** Annapurna Labs is the part of Amazon that designs the custom silicon behind the cloud, including Trainium for AI training, Graviton CPUs, and the AWS Nitro system. Nearly every server in AWS runs hardware we designed. We're a new team inside Annapurna Trainium Systems taking Trainium beyond AWS, so customers can run it in their own data centers. **What do we do?** We build the software that runs on Trainium servers in customers' own data centers. We also build the software customers use to install, provision, operate, update, and monitor those servers. We give the people who run this hardware a complete way to stand it up, watch its health, deliver new software to it, and diagnose it, all through open, standard interfaces. We own that software from design through the running system. **Why it's high-impact?** The hardware is just silicon until our software makes it provisionable, observable, and serviceable. Every system runs through what we build. The service you own is on the path for all of them, and the people who run this hardware depend on it every day. **What's the challenge?** There are many ambiguous and difficult challenges in our fast-moving space. Our services require deep system and software expertise. You need to have the ability to work within a fast moving and startup-like environment in a large company. You will identify solutions, trying ideas, given space to fail and iterate to produce products that your customers love. **What you will do?** You own a large component of the software that manages servers, racks, and clusters from outside. That might be a provisioning plugin, a telemetry exporter, or the service that delivers software updates. It might also be a test suite every release passes, or the tool that walks a customer through a repair. Some of it works against the server's interfaces, and some of it never touches hardware. You design it with direction from your lead and run it in production. **Who would succeed in this role?** An engineer who builds and operates a service in production and takes a large component from design to running code with some direction. You read logs and reason across process and system boundaries, you ship in small verifiable steps, and you start to mentor the engineers around you. Key job responsibilities - Own the design and implementation of a large component or service in the management plane, in provisioning, monitoring, telemetry, software delivery, or diagnostics. - Make the application-level trade-offs on your component, and seek direction on the calls that reach beyond it. - Automate and simplify the team's development, test, and operations work, and mentor peers as you grow. - work backward from customer requirements and deliver solutions that are simple. A day in the life You design and build the provisioning and management surface over standard interfaces like Redfish, and the boot flow operator tools drive. You build the offline software-update service and prove the signed bundle applies and recovers cleanly. You design each system against the interfaces the platform exposes and turn architecture decisions into APIs and tools a customer runs without you in the loop. About the team Our team builds the software suite for provisioning, monitoring, software delivery, and the diagnostics of Trainium systems, and we build all of it on open, standard interfaces. We serve the engineers and operators who run large-scale AI training and need to provision, monitor, update, and troubleshoot it on their own terms. We own it end to end.

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

Build the AI that runs a robot factory.

We build every Tutor robot ourselves, in our own factory in Watertown, MA, and we're on our way to building more than 1,000 of them. That factory already runs on software we made ourselves, and we use AI every day to plan what to build, spot problems, and keep quality high. Now we need someone to own those tools full time.

Your job in one sentence: build AI tools that the people on our factory floor use every shift, and keep them working.

The basics

  • Team: Manufacturing
  • Your boss: Head of Manufacturing
  • Where: Onsite in Watertown, MA. You'll sit on the factory floor, not in an office down the hall.
  • Type: Full-time
  • Pay: $150,000 to $190,000 a year, plus equity

Our offerings range from self-service claim-filing software to advanced backend fraud detection systems. We power claims processing for some of the largest insurers globally, tackling complex challenges such as creating digital experiences that offer clarity and comfort to claimants during stressful times and orchestrating large-scale machine learning-driven decision-making on billions of dollars in claims payments. At Assured, the work environment is dynamic, collaborative, and rewarding, where great decisions are driven by data rather than intuition. About The Role As a Staff Data Analyst at Assured, you will play a pivotal role in partnering with cross-functional teams to transform raw data into meaningful insights that drive smarter business decisions. You will help leaders understand business performance, identify opportunities for improvement, and measure the impact of strategic initiatives. This role goes beyond reporting historical data; you will analyze the reasons behind business outcomes and recommend actionable next steps. You will design and analyze experiments, build dashboards, identify trends, and improve data quality to empower confident decision-making across the organization. Your work will provide visibility into operational performance, customer outcomes, and organizational health, ultimately guiding business strategy and enhancing operational efficiency. Qualifications Proven experience using data to drive business decisions and solve complex problems through analysis. Strong analytical fundamentals, with proficiency in SQL and comfort working with large datasets. Ability to think beyond reporting by investigating root causes, identifying opportunities, and recommending actionable solutions. Excellent communication skills, capable of explaining analytical findings to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. Experience solving ambiguous problems by defining appropriate data, analyses, and metrics without predefined reports. Adaptability to new tools and technologies with a focus on problem-solving rather than reliance on specific platforms. Familiarity with modern analytics tools such as Python, R, Tableau, Power BI, Looker, AWS, Snowflake, or Databricks is a plus but not required. Responsibilities Design and analyze experiments, pilots, and performance evaluations to isolate impactful initiatives and support confident decision-making. Build and maintain dashboards and reports that provide leaders with clear visibility into operational and organizational performance. Analyze data from multiple sources to identify trends, emerging opportunities, risks, and areas for improvement. Use segmentation, cohort analysis, and behavioral data to understand customers, users, or operational processes and identify optimization opportunities. Collaborate with stakeholders across departments to answer critical business questions, evaluate tradeoffs, and provide data-driven recommendations. Improve data quality, instrumentation, and reporting by identifying gaps in data collection and helping teams capture necessary information. Develop meaningful metrics and reporting frameworks that enable consistent measurement of success and progress tracking over time. Identify opportunities to enhance business processes, customer experiences, and operational efficiency through thoughtful data analysis. Communicate complex analytical insights clearly to influence strategy and decision-making throughout the organization. Benefits Competitive salary and equity packages for all employees. Health Flexible Spending Accounts (FSAs) and Health Savings Accounts (HSAs) for pre-tax medical expenses. Regular team events and offsites to foster connection despite a remote work environment. jobs.jd_excerpt: About Softprobe Softprobe builds quality infrastructure for AI agents. We're a US/China developer-tools startup working on the business layer of AI agent quality — not infra, but whether agents actually do the right thing for real users. One of our business-layer evals, for example, is customer emotion detection. We build in the open. Our two open-source products: Arex — automated API testing that captures real user traffic and replays it as test cases. No hand-written test suites to maintain, no costly throwaway test environments. Trusted by teams at Trip.com, Yeahka, United Imaging, Lexin, ZTO, and others. thelake — an open-source AI evidence lake on DuckDB, a LangSmith / Datadog alternative built for long-term storage of full payloads (prompts, responses, tool I/O, HTTP bodies) as open Parquet — about 200x cheaper than index-heavy observability. OTLP in, DuckDB SQL out. It's the durable evidence foundation underneath Softprobe Agent QA. What you'll do Build and ship across both products: Arex's traffic-capture and replay engine, and thelake's OTLP ingest, DuckLake storage, and query layer. Build the business-layer evaluation surface of Softprobe Agent QA — evals, Explorer, diagnosis, and collaboration on top of the evidence lake. Design evals that judge agents on business outcomes, not just token-level metrics — and make the results explainable to the teams running the agents. Work directly with real agent traffic from production systems, including replaying and regressing against recorded sessions. We're looking for An expert in AI agents — this is the core requirement. You've built, shipped, and debugged LLM-powered agents in production, not just demos. You know how agents fail in practice (bad tool calls, lost context, wrong escalation, hallucinated confidence) and how to measure and fix that. Strong backend engineering fundamentals, and comfort owning a feature end to end — from design through production. Experience with LLM evaluation: building evals, benchmarks, or red-teaming, and turning evaluation results into product improvements. Familiarity with observability and tracing (OpenTelemetry, structured logging, trace analysis) and with data systems for large-scale storage and querying. Nice to have Open-source contributions, especially in testing, observability, or agent frameworks. Experience with replay / record-and-replay testing systems. Rust and/or Java, DuckDB, and columnar storage (Parquet). Experience with customer-facing AI (support, sales, or service agents) and the quality bar those users expect. Our stack Java (Arex) · Rust (thelake) · DuckDB / DuckLake · OpenTelemetry · MongoDB · Redis

jobs.jd_excerpt: Mirage is an AI video company focused on making creation dramatically easier. Our team tackles some of the hardest creative and technical challenges in generative media. We get to rethink how people collaborate with AI that can actually do creative work with them—defining entirely new interaction paradigms for AI-native video tools. We make that possible by building multimodal agents that turn creative direction into edits, rendering engines that composite multiple layers of video and graphics, and generative video models trained from the ground up that create new media when needed. All of this comes together in Captions, our creative workspace for generating, editing, and designing video. The technology behind Captions is now available more broadly: Tesseract gives any AI agent native video-editing capabilities, while developers can integrate our models into their own products through APIs. Explore our work Captions — Our flagship creative workspace Tesseract — Our professional video engine for AI agents Research — The foundation models we build in-house Updates — The latest from Mirage TechCrunch , Forbes , Fast Company — Press Our Investors We’re very fortunate to have some the best investors and entrepreneurs backing us, including Index Ventures, Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, Andreessen Horowitz, General Catalyst , Uncommon Projects, Kevin Systrom, Mike Krieger, Lenny Rachitsky, Antoine Martin, Julie Zhuo, Ben Rubin, Jaren Glover, SVAngel, 20VC, Ludlow Ventures, Chapter One, and more. Please note that most of our roles will require you to be in-person at our NYC HQ (located in Union Square) About the role We want Tesseract to render 3D that is indistinguishable from footage. You'll be the founding engineer for photoreal 3D in Tesseract, our Rust-based, cross-platform graphics and media rendering engine. Tesseract already renders video, motion graphics, effects and compositing in a color- managed pipeline. You'll build 3D to the same standard: a fast interactive preview for editing, and a physically based final render, path-traced or hybrid ray-traced, that produces film-quality frames for export. Both run from one scene, material and lighting model, so what people see while they edit is what they export. Scenes are authored by people and by AI agents, so render cost, failure modes and APIs matter as much as image quality. This is a foundational role: you'll make the core architectural decisions and help build the team around them. What you'll do Define the architecture for photoreal 3D: how ray tracing, rasterization and denoising divide the work, and how that maps onto Metal, Vulkan, Direct3D and WebGPU. Build light transport: global illumination, reflections and refraction, soft shadows from area lights, and volumetrics such as haze, fog and light shafts. Build a physically based model for materials, lights and cameras: energy-conserving materials (metal, glass, clearcoat, sheen, translucency), lights in real-world units, and a camera with exposure, depth of field and motion blur. Own image quality: sampling, antialiasing, accumulation, denoising and firefly suppression, with frames that stay stable and deterministic across a video export. Scale scenes to production complexity with acceleration structures, instancing, culling and memory management, for millions of triangles and tens of thousands of objects. Integrate 3D into Tesseract's video, motion graphics and compositing pipeline, including ACES color management and render passes such as depth, normals, motion vectors and light groups. Make render cost predictable and rendering robust: performance budgets, profiling, and headless batch rendering on local and cloud GPUs. Design 3D APIs that work for people and AI agents alike: a clear scene representation, actionable validation errors, fast previews and render cost known before the render. Work with engine, product and AI teams, and help hire and grow the 3D rendering team. What makes you a great fit Deep experience building physically based renderers in production: film or offline renderers, path tracers, or game engines with ray-traced or hybrid lighting. Strong command of light transport: the rendering equation, Monte Carlo integration, importance sampling, material models and denoising. Hands-on GPU ray tracing: building and traversing acceleration structures (BVHs), hardware ray-tracing APIs such as Metal ray tracing, Vulkan ray tracing or DXR, and compute-based fallbacks. A solid understanding of modern rasterization pipelines, and of how hybrid renderers combine rasterization with ray tracing. Hands-on experience with Metal, Vulkan, Direct3D or WebGPU, including compute shaders, GPU profiling and GPU debugging. Proficiency in Rust or C++, with strong reasoning about memory, concurrency and performance. Strong foundations in the mathematics of graphics: linear algebra, geometry, probability and sampling. An eye for realism: you can look at a frame, say why it doesn't read as real, and fix the cause. Experience owning complex technical projects and making architectural decisions in ambiguous problem spaces. Even better if… You've worked on the internals of a production renderer or engine such as Cycles, Arnold, RenderMan, V-Ray, Karma, Unreal Engine (Lumen or its path tracer) or Unity HDRP. You've built or integrated ML denoisers, or worked on neural rendering. You've worked with color management (ACES, OpenColorIO), HDR output or film-look pipelines. You've built on cross-platform graphics abstractions such as wgpu, including extending them where they lack features such as ray tracing. You've optimized rendering for Apple silicon or mobile GPUs. You have experience with Rust, video compositing, or integrating 2D and 3D rendering in creative tools. jobs.jd_excerpt: Superhuman offers a dynamic hybrid working model for this role. This flexible approach gives team members the best of both worlds: plenty of focus time along with in-person collaboration that helps foster trust, innovation, and a strong team culture. Preferred locations for team members for our Data Platform roles are our San Francisco or Seattle hubs. About Superhuman Grammarly is now part of Superhuman, the AI productivity platform on a mission to unlock the superhuman potential in everyone. The Superhuman suite of apps and agents brings AI wherever people work, integrating with over 1 million applications and websites. The company's products include Grammarly's writing assistance, Docs’ collaborative workspace, Mail's inbox management, and Go, the proactive AI assistant that understands context and delivers help automatically. Founded in 2009, Superhuman empowers over 40 million people, 50,000 organizations, and 3,000 educational institutions worldwide to eliminate busywork and focus on what matters. Learn more at superhuman.com and about our values here. The Opportunity As a Data Engineer on the Business Unit (BU) Pod supporting Go , you’ll build the pipelines and data models that help us understand how people use Superhuman’s proactive AI assistant. You’ll work closely with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to give teams the data they need to improve the product and measure its impact. Go helps people where they already work, through conversations, inline suggestions, and built-in and custom agents. Understanding how people use these experiences takes more than counting clicks. Your work will help teams see where users get stuck, which capabilities they find useful, and what brings them back. It will also help connect Go’s usage to customer adoption and business growth. You’ll own projects and datasets with a clear scope, supported by experienced engineers. Most of your work will focus on production pipelines and reusable data models that teams can use to answer their own questions. You’ll also contribute analysis and dashboards when they help move a decision forward. As you learn the product and our systems, you’ll have opportunities to take on more complex work. What You’ll Do Build and maintain production data pipelines in Databricks that process product events, user activity, and agent interactions across Go. Develop datasets for onboarding, activation, engagement, retention, and conversion so teams can work from consistent metrics. Work with Product, Engineering, and Data Science to define what needs to be measured, improve event logging, and check that new features are represented correctly in downstream data. Make data models easy to understand and use, with clear definitions and documentation that support self-service through analytics and AI tools. Build focused analyses and dashboards when they help partners use the data or make a decision. Connect Go usage with customer and account data to help teams understand adoption, customer value, and Go’s contribution to growth and revenue. Keep the datasets you own accurate, up-to-date, and reliable. Add tests and monitoring, investigate discrepancies, and fix the underlying causes. Improve pipeline and query performance, manage compute costs, and make the code you work on easier to maintain. You’ll work alongside engineers and partners across Data Platform and Go. We care about understanding the problem, questioning assumptions, and following through when the answer takes some digging. You’ll contribute to design decisions and have teammates to turn to as you build your expertise. Qualifications You have 2+ years of experience building and operating production data pipelines, ideally for product analytics or other critical business use cases. You’re highly proficient in SQL and have experience writing, debugging, and optimizing transformations in a modern lakehouse or cloud data warehouse such as Databricks or Snowflake. You understand data modeling and warehouse design, and can turn complex source data into tables that others can understand and reuse. You test your work carefully, investigate unexpected results, and trace data issues back to their source. You have experience with workflow orchestration, version control, and deployment practices for data pipelines, using tools such as Databricks Workflows, Airflow, and Git. You use AI-assisted development tools such as Codex, Claude Code, or Cursor, and take responsibility for testing and validating the code they produce. You communicate clearly with technical and nontechnical partners. You can turn a product question into data requirements and explain the assumptions and limitations behind an answer. You’re curious about how people use products and how your work can help teams make better decisions. You follow your work through to production, break problems into manageable steps, raise risks and dependencies early, and ask for help when you need it. Nice to have Experience using Python and/or Spark for data transformations, pipelines, or automation. Experience with product or growth analytics, including adoption funnels, retention, conversion, or A/B experiments. Experience working with event logging and behavioral data from web, desktop, or mobile products. Experience supporting AI products or agents, including measuring adoption, interaction quality, reliability, latency, or usage costs. Experience building dashboards or other data tools that product, analytics, and business teams use to answer their own questions. Compensation And Benefits Superhuman offers all team members competitive pay along with a benefits package encompassing the following and more: Excellent health care (including a wide range of medical, dental, vision, mental health, and fertility benefits) Disability and life insurance options 401(k) and RRSP matching Paid parental leave 20 days of paid time off per year, 12 days of paid holidays per year, two floating holidays per year, and flexible sick time

The immediate challenge is building an agent that is both highly accurate and broadly trusted. Experienced incident responders need a transparent collaborator that helps them investigate, continuously surfaces relevant evidence, and keeps them in control. Engineers who encounter incidents only occasionally need an agent that leads the investigation and guides them to a safe outcome. You will lead two tightly connected areas: - Agent quality - skills, tools, context, memory, offline evaluation, backtesting, online experimentation, and learning from production outcomes. - Responder experience - a multi-turn interface that gives responders visibility into the agent's work and brings together the operational data they need to make decisions. This is a deeply hands-on technical leadership role at the intersection of large-scale distributed systems, incident response, applied AI, and product engineering. You will personally design and ship critical parts of the system while leading senior engineers across team and organizational boundaries. jobs.jd_excerpt:
E11 Bio is on a mission to advance connectomics towards the scale of whole mammalian brains. We are a collaborative and interdisciplinary team of scientists and engineers engaged in a neuroscience moonshot project to develop a radical technology platform for scalable brain mapping. E11 Bio is a non-profit Convergent Research focused research organization located in Alameda, California, pursuing blue-skies neuroscience research yet operating like a nimble, tight-knit start-up. Read our technology roadmap. 

We are seeking a creative and mission-driven Machine Learning Scientist to develop scalable automatic proofreading methods leveraging barcode and shape information. In this role, you will own core ML pipelines for automated proofreading of neuron and synaptic reconstructions in optical connectomics datasets, working closely with wet lab scientists, microscopists, and domain experts to ensure biological fidelity and scalability. Your work will directly support E11’s goal of making reliable connectomic data accessible to the broader neuroscience community.

In this role you will be focused on decreasing segmentation and proofreading costs for optical connectomics datasets that we are generating at E11, a critical bottleneck in the connectomics field. You will be responsible for improving initial segmentations using large spatial contexts with rich data features, and ingesting resulting datasets into scalable proofreading software for dissemination to the scientific community.

jobs.jd_excerpt:
The EC2 Capacity Telemetry and Autonomous Systems team is looking for an experienced Software Development Engineer to join our Seattle-based team. EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud) is part of Amazon Web Services, the global leader in public cloud infrastructure. We build the systems that measure what EC2's capacity is doing in real time — what exists, what is in use, what is reserved, and where demand is going unmet — detect when any of it moves, establish why, and increasingly act on it without a person in the loop. We sit within a group of software engineers and scientists who build the forecasting algorithms and modeling systems that determine how EC2 is built and packed, so that capacity is maximally utilized and maximally available through automated capacity planning and optimization. Those models run on what our systems measure, and the decisions they produce are executed by software we own. This is a software engineering team at the crossroads of writing our own systems and operating the best of open source. We design and run distributed services with real availability and latency commitments. We build low-latency query and serving layers on engines such as Apache Druid, ClickHouse and Apache Pinot, and extend them where our workload outgrows what they do out of the box. We write optimization and decision engines that replace work people were doing by hand. We build APIs that other services depend on, and the React web applications that operators and planners run their day from. And we build agentic systems on top of all of it, so a problem gets diagnosed and resolved by software rather than escalated to a human with a chart attached. The work is operationally real. Our consumers are live systems, and ours matter most at exactly the moments something else is going wrong, so availability is a design constraint here rather than something handled after launch. Key job responsibilities - Design, build, launch and operate production services end to end — you will write the design document, make the trade-offs, defend them in review, and own what you shipped - Build high-throughput distributed systems that operate under real latency and availability commitments, and the query and serving layers behind them - Build real-time detection and alerting that tells an operator what changed and why it matters, rather than requiring them to know what to look for first - Build rules and decision engines that replace large-scale manual workflows with software - Build optimization systems that return the best available answer within a fixed time budget, degrading to a simpler strategy rather than failing - Build and extend the APIs other services depend on, and the React web applications our operators and planners work in - Build agentic systems that investigate a problem, determine the cause, recommend a course of action and increasingly take it - Raise the operational bar on what you own: monitoring, alarming, recovery paths and the tests that span service boundaries A day in the life Your day is a mix of building and deciding. A typical week has you deep in implementation on a service you own, in a design review arguing about someone else's, and in a conversation with the people who depend on what you build. Your closest collaborators are the engineers and scientists who build the forecasting and optimization models next to you — they need what your systems produce, and what they produce has to land in systems you operate. Beyond the immediate team you will work with capacity planners and operators who make decisions from the software you build, with partner service teams whose systems you integrate with and occasionally contribute code to directly, and with the leadership who review the operational numbers your systems generate. You will be expected to take on ambiguous problems and work independently, making business and technical trade-offs to deliver results — with support from teammates who will answer questions and work through day-to-day problems with you. Where no established pattern exists, we evaluate options, choose one, and write down why. You will be a fully participating team member in daily stand-ups, design review sessions, demos, code reviews and other team gatherings. This position involves on-call responsibilities, typically one week every two months. We build fault-tolerant systems to minimize being paged during off-hours, and when we are paged we root-cause and fix so the same page does not come back. About the team Our mission is that EC2 capacity is maximally available and maximally utilized, managed autonomously rather than by hand. Every system we build moves work from a person to software and then makes that software accountable for the outcome. We set tenets and target outcomes before a design exists, then build against them and settle the trade-offs in review. Design, implementation, prototyping, security review and documentation rotate across the team, so no system has a single point of knowledge and engineers end a year with more range than they began it. We are invested in your growth. We assign projects that balance what the business needs against what will make each engineer more capable of owning something larger next time. As an experienced engineer you will have opportunities to mentor while working alongside senior and principal engineers across the organization. As a team, we enjoy connecting socially while respecting the balance between work and personal life.
